**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 74 **Archetype** [Avenging Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=338) **Prerequisites** [Avenging Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8139) --- You have managed to gain a degree of control over the runelord’s ancient soul within your mind, enough that you can project this invasive influence into the minds of others. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). You attempt to send your runelord’s influence into the mind of a creature you can sense within 30 feet. The creature attempts a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Giants take a –2 status penalty to this saving throw. Regardless of the result, the target is temporarily immune to this ability for 24 hours once the Subjugation ends. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as it fights off your runelord’s influence. You gain awareness of its abilities and weaknesses as if you achieved a critical success on a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check to identify the creature.
**Failure** The creature relinquishes control of its faculties and abilities. You gain awareness of its abilities and weaknesses as success. You [control](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) the creature until the end of its next turn.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but you control the creature for 1 minute.

[Submerged Stillness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8994) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 19

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

With a mix of magic and physical training, you have learned to render yourself [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) while hiding underwater. You mimic the subtle movement of water so as not to disturb its surface, and you change your skin color to blend in with your surroundings. You gain the effects of [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577) for up to 1 hour, as long as you remain submerged.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs=""
>
[Subtle Shank](/Feats.aspx?ID=2208) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

**Prerequisites**
[Quick Draw](/Feats.aspx?ID=498)

**Access**
Help either the Washboard Dogs or the Diobel Sweepers destroy their rival.

**Requirements**
You have a melee weapon of light bulk [Concealed](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) on your person via the [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) skill, and the target isn't aware of it.

</column>

---

You draw a concealed weapon, attack with it, and then hide it away again in one smooth motion. Interact to draw the weapon, Strike with that weapon, and then Conceal it with a Stealth check. The target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) for this attack.

<title level="2">Gang Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

Street gangs in Absalom recruit amateur pickpockets, ruffians, and vandals who show promise in their specialties and operate well in tight groups.

 Rogue agents can gain access to some of the following rogue feats by successfully helping Maurrisa Jonne or Bloody Berleth eliminate their rival (see Chapter 1). Some of these feats, however, can be gained only by helping a particular side in the gang conflict.

**Related Feats**: [Ambushing Knockdown](/Feats.aspx?ID=2207), [Coordinated Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=2210), [Deny Support](/Feats.aspx?ID=2209), [Slice and Swipe](/Feats.aspx?ID=2206)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Subtle Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9358) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

You’ve learned how to hide your meddling from the casters of spells you’re shifting. If your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check when Shifting a Spell is greater than its caster’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC, you can prevent the caster from learning the effects of the shift you’re attempting to apply. On a critical success, they don’t become aware that you’re applying a shift at all (although the effect of the shift might still give you away).

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 263

Trained in [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17)

</column>

---

When you successfully Steal something, observers (creatures other than the creature you stole from) take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Perception DCs to detect your theft. Additionally, if you first Create a Diversion using Deception, taking a single Palm an Object or Steal action doesn’t end your undetected condition.

<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 46

**Archetype** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=246)

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6302)

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet fails a Will saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect.

</column>

---

You expect the same level of urbane sophistication from your allies as you possess, so whenever one of them succumbs to egregious behavior from a mental effect, you're immediately mortified. How dare they make you look bad! Whether you respond with noisy contempt or quiet distress, your reaction gives your ally a second chance to shake off the effect and save the moment, at least socially. Your ally rerolls the triggering Will saving throw with a +1 circumstance bonus and uses the higher result. Regardless of the result of the save, your ally is temporarily immune to Such a Disgrace! for 10 minutes.

[Sudden Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=155) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 149

</column>

---

You make an impressive leap and swing while you soar. Make a [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) and attempt one melee Strike at any point during your jump. Immediately after the Strike, you fall to the ground if you're in the air, even if you haven't reached the maximum distance of your jump. If the distance you fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright.

 When attempting a High Jump or Long Jump during a Sudden Leap, determine the DC using the Long Jump DCs, and increase your maximum distance to double your Speed.

**Special** If you have [Felling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=390), you can spend 3 actions to make a Sudden Leap and use Felling Strike instead of a normal Strike.

---

You leverage your body’s amorphous nature to spook others. Attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) a creature within 30 feet. Demoralize loses the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait and gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait, and you don’t take a penalty if the creature doesn’t understand your language. If you were hidden to the creature, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check, and if you succeed, the creature is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2 instead of frightened 1. All creatures that witnessed you use Sudden Terror are then temporarily immune to your Sudden Terror for 24 hours.

</column>

---

Your elemental ancestor was a [janni](/Monsters.aspx?ID=211), genies that walk the mortal world and embody all four elements together. You inherited a janni's nature as a wanderer and ability to survive in many types of environment, from the hottest desert to the coldest tundra. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). If you would automatically become trained in Survival (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the [Forager](/Feats.aspx?ID=786) skill feat as a bonus feat.

When you cast _summon instrument_, you can modify its duration to be sustained, up to 1 minute. When you do, you summon a number of instruments equal to your spellcasting ability modifier that hover around you and play of their own accord. The target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Summoner](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=96)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14

</column>

---

You've formed a bond with an eidolon, an entity that manifests in a physical body only through its link to your life force. Your bond may be tenuous, but that doesn't make your connection any less special. You gain an [eidolon](/Eidolons.aspx) as well as the Manifest Eidolon activity. Due to your tenuous link, you can't gain or use [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) actions. Because you don't have [Act Together](/Actions.aspx?ID=758), only you or your eidolon can perform an exploration activity at one time, so for instance you couldn't both be [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) or [Investigating](/Actions.aspx?ID=516).

 Your eidolon is trained in [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks and unarmored defense, and shares your proficiency rank for Perception, saving throws, and skill checks. Choose an eidolon type. You become trained in your eidolon's listed skills. For each of those skills that you are already trained in, you become trained in a different skill of your choice. Your eidolon's initial ability scores are reduced. It starts with a 16 in any ability score listed at 18 for its eidolon array. It otherwise gains the statistics listed for an eidolon of that type.

 At 5th level, the eidolon's ability score that was reduced to 16 increases to 18, before applying ability boosts. At levels 5, 10, 15, and 20, your eidolon also gets four ability boosts, which follow the same rules as yours.

<document level="2" id="action-757" />

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the summoner archetype.

<title level="2">Summoner Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Summoner Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=2957), [Basic Synergy](/Feats.aspx?ID=2954), [Expert Combat Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=2958), [Initial Eidolon Ability](/Feats.aspx?ID=2955)

---

You’ve formed a bond with an eidolon, an entity that manifests in a physical body only through their link to your life force. You gain an [eidolon](/Eidolons.aspx) as well as the [Manifest Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757) activity. Due to your tenuous link, you can’t gain or use [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) actions. Because you don’t have [Act Together](/Actions.aspx?ID=758), only you or your eidolon can perform an [exploration](/Rules.aspx?ID=2006) activity at one time.

    right="Feat 6"

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 101

**Archetype** [Bright Lion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=129)

**Prerequisites**
[Bright Lion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2172)

</column>

---

The [Old Sun Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=19) have granted you a gift in your fight against [Walkena](/Deities.aspx?ID=159). You gain the [_sun's fury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=818) focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to pray to the Old Sun Gods; if you already have a focus pool, increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1. Your Bright Lion focus spells are divine spells; when you gain this feat, if you aren't already, you become trained in divine spell attacks and spell DCs, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability score.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

[Winged Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5527)

**Requirements**
You’re in [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407)

</column>

---

By keeping your feathers clean and sleek, you can catch the light across your wings to create a startling glare in the eyes of a creature within 20 feet. The target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure). Regardless of their result, the target is temporarily immune to Sunbird Glare for 10 minutes.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sunder Enchantment](/Feats.aspx?ID=1627) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 111

**Prerequisites**
[Sunder Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1624)

</column>

---

You can focus your superstition to break the magic of an item, in addition to destroying freestanding spells and those active on creatures. When you Sunder a Spell, you can instead attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) either an unattended magic item or one of your target's magic items. If your counteract attempt succeeds, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. If you target an [artifact](/Equipment.aspx?Category=45), an [intelligent item](/Equipment.aspx?Category=48), or a particularly powerful item, your counteract attempt automatically fails.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sunder Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1624) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=135" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 111

**Prerequisites**
[superstition instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

You draw upon your superstitious fury to destroy a spell. Make a Strike with a melee weapon or an unarmed attack against a creature, object, or a spell manifestation (such as the wall created by [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362) or the guardian from [_spiritual guardian_](/Spells.aspx?ID=305)). If you're targeting something that doesn't have an AC listed, its AC is usually 10 against this Strike for targets that are very easy to hit, like a wall, or a different AC determined by the GM. If your Strike hits, you can attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) a single spell or magical effect on the target. Your counteract level for this attempt is equal to half your level rounded up, and you use the result of your attack roll for the counteract check.

 Whether or not you succeed at your Strike, the target becomes temporarily immune to your Sunder Spell for 24 hours.

<title level="2">Sunder Spell leads to...</title>
[Sunder Enchantment](/Feats.aspx?ID=1627)

</title>

---

Whether in the salon or on the street, you've captured the attention of everyone around you. In this moment, they're all hanging on your next word or anticipating your next move. You capture the moment by striking an unforgettable pose, one that your friends find alluring and your foes find alarming. Roll a Diplomacy or Intimidation check. You can substitute the result of this check for one Reflex save you would be required to attempt in the next minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sunlit Vitality](/Feats.aspx?ID=4315) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ardande" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=498" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 48

</column>

---

You gain nourishment through photosynthesis, like trees and other green plants. You typically don't need to pay for food, though you begin to [starve](/Rules.aspx?ID=537) if you go without sunlight for 1 week. You can derive nourishment from specially formulated bottles of sunlight instead of natural sunlight, but these bottles cost 10 times as much as standard rations (4 gp per week).

[Superimpose Time Duplicates](/Feats.aspx?ID=3851) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 186

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**

---

You call alternate versions of yourself, either from a different timeline or perhaps yourself from a different point in your current timeline, to aid you in combat. Until the start of your next turn, these alternate selves flicker in and out in your vicinity, providing flanking for you against all enemies within your reach. Flanking with your time duplicates is the same as flanking with an ally and so is subject to effects like [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=1) or the deny advantage class feature.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Superior Propulsion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3150) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 57

**Archetype** [Vehicle Mechanic](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=113)

**Prerequisites**
[Vehicle Mechanic Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3147)

</column>

---

By experimenting with the effects of momentum gained from your signature [vehicle's](/Vehicles.aspx) movement, you have learned to get more from propulsion than just speed when the pilot pushes the vehicle to its limit. Each time the pilot [Drives](/Actions.aspx?ID=483) your signature vehicle as a 2- or 3-action activity and succeeds at the Piloting check, the vehicle produces an additional effect, depending on its method of propulsion. If your signature vehicle has more than one propulsion method, the pilot can select which benefit to gain each time they succeed at the Piloting check to Drive the vehicle as a 2- or 3-action activity.

 **Alchemical** The caustic runoff from the alchemical engines is now weaponized. Creatures adjacent to your signature vehicle when it begins its movement take acid damage equal to your level.

 **Clockwork** More resilient gears allow the vehicle to remain functional, even when damaged. If your signature vehicle is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2), it does not need to make the flat check to avoid losing operating time.

 **Magical** The residual magic from your signature vehicle interferes with hostile spells. Pilots, crew, and passengers of the vehicle gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells until the start of the pilot's next turn.

 **Pulled** You have eased the amount of effort needed for those pulling your signature vehicle to move it. The vehicle gains a +10 circumstance bonus to its Speed.

 **Rowed** Reinforced ports protect the rowers below decks from harm. Rowers of your signature vehicle who are below decks have greater cover from attacks from outside the vehicle and are not damaged when the vehicle takes collision damage.

 **Steam** The outlet of steam forms a cloud around the vehicle as it moves. For the duration of its movement, your signature vehicle is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4).

 **Wind** The draft of the wind helps the vehicle turn. During this movement, your signature vehicle can turn normally, rather than needing to move in a straight line as normal for a 2- or 3-action Drive.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 77

</column>

---

Your senses are peerless. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks, and you gain [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=416). If you already have low-light vision, gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) instead. Furthermore, when you target an enemy, you automatically succeed at the flat check if that enemy is concealed, hidden, or undetected.

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Supertaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=2152) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 209

**Prerequisites**
master in Perception

</column>

---

You have refined your palate and have a discerning sense of taste that can detect abnormalities in the flavor and texture of food and beverages. When eating food or drinking a beverage, you automatically attempt to identify the ingredients, which might alert you to the presence of alterations or additives, such as [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126). The GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) Perception check using the poison's level to determine the DC; on a success, you learn that the food or drink was poisoned, but not the specific poison used. 

If you lick or taste something while [Investigating](/Actions.aspx?ID=516) or attempting to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) to identify something, if the taste would provide relevant additional information (at the GM's discretion), you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check.

[Suplex](/Feats.aspx?ID=3397) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Wrestler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=127)

**Prerequisites**
[Wrestler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3394)

**Requirements**
You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33).

</column>

---

Flexing your entire body, you heave your opponent over your head and slam them into the ground. Make an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) melee Strike against the creature you have grabbed or restrained; on a success, the target lands [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), and on a critical success, the target lands prone and takes an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage. Regardless of whether the Strike is successful, you immediately release your hold on the target.

You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to skill checks to move within your favored terrain, such as [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) on ice, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) in rough water, Acrobatics checks to [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) in windy conditions, and so forth.

>
[Surface Tension](/Feats.aspx?ID=7468) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=732" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 83

**Prerequisites**
[Resurgent Maelstrom Hybrid Study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=9)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding a broken weapon.

</column>

---

You encase the pieces of your broken weapon together with water you pull from the surrounding environment. The weapon’s broken condition is temporarily suppressed, and the weapon deals an additional amount of bludgeoning damage equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice; this damage can’t be changed to any other type. The weapon also gains the deadly d8 trait; if the weapon already had the [deadly](/Traits.aspx?ID=570) trait, the damage die increases by one step or to d8, whichever is higher. The first time you use this weapon to Spellstrike or get a critical success on an attack with it, the weapon is completely destroyed.

 If the weapon has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it’s an artifact, cursed item, or other item that’s difficult to break or destroy, it is not destroyed, and this ability only lasts until the end of your turn.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 112 **Prerequisites** [forensic medicine methodology](/Methodologies.aspx?ID=7) --- With a few well-placed jabs with your fist or weapon, you render your opponent disoriented or ungainly. Attempt a [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check against the Fortitude DC of a target within your reach. The result of your check determines the severity of the condition you inflict. **Critical Success** The target is either [clumsy 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) or [stupefied 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) until the end of your next turn. The target is then immune to Surgical Shock for 1 hour.
**Success** As critical success, but the target is either clumsy 2 or stupefied 2.
**Failure** The target is minorly inconvenienced. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the next attack action you attempt against it before the end of your turn.
**Critical Failure** The target is unaffected and you overextend yourself, triggering reactions as if you had used a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) action.

With a complex gesture, you focus the divine power of your spell to overcome enemies' resistances. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores an amount of the target's resistance equal to your level against all the following types of damage: chaotic, evil, good, lawful, negative, and positive. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell, such as the positive energy within a [_field of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=114). This doesn't cause the spell to ignore immunities, only resistances.

Lashing forward, your weapon becomes an extension of your nexus, washing your enemies in a torrent of magical fury. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167). Regardless of the result, you create a 30- foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) of magical energy dealing 3d6 force damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save against your nexus DC. You choose the cone’s direction, but its first square must be a square in the target of your strike’s space. A creature that critically fails the save is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). The force damage increases by 1d6 at 8th level and every 2 levels thereafter. You are no longer overflowing.

---

Either through the tales of elders in your settlement or through the messages thumped by those who oversaw your generation dig, you hold the knowledge of many surkis before you. You become trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) and the skill associated with the magical tradition from your magiphage ability ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) for [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) for [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) for [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) for [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. 

You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for [Surki Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8).

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 83

</column>

---

Your eidolon jumps into the air to attack a foe. Your eidolon makes a [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) and attempts one melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) at any point during that jump. Immediately after the Strike, your eidolon falls to the ground if they’re in the air, even if they haven’t reached the maximum distance of their jump. If the distance your eidolon falls is no more than the height of their jump, your eidolon takes no damage and lands upright.

When attempting a High Jump or Long Jump during a Surprising Leap, determine the jump distance using Long Jump’s rules, and change your eidolon’s maximum distance to double their Speed.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Survey Wildlife](/Feats.aspx?ID=5221) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 263

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You can study details in the wilderness to determine the presence of nearby creatures. You can spend 10 minutes assessing the area around you to find out what creatures are nearby, based on nests, scat, and marks on vegetation. Attempt a Survival check against a DC determined by the GM based on how obvious the signs are. On a success, you can attempt a Recall Knowledge check with a –2 penalty to learn more about the creatures just from these signs. If you’re a master in Survival, you don’t take the penalty

<title

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Survivor of Desolation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1099) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 95

**Archetype** [Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097)

</column>

---

You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against unnatural weather events or environmental hazards occurring in blighted or otherwise unnaturally marred regions. If you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead; if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. This does not apply to unnatural events created or directed by active effects, such as spells that create anomalous weather or hazardous areas.

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Suspect of Opportunity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1470) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 63

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Trigger**
A foe takes a hostile action against you in combat.

</column>

---

Sometimes something intrudes upon your case unexpectedly, such as an ambush sent to bring your investigation to a close. You've learned how to compartmentalize your main lead and pursue a new one for your current predicament. You [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=544) against the triggering foe, setting aside but not ending one of your currently active leads, if you have two leads. At the end of the combat encounter, you stop Pursuing the Lead against the triggering foe and return to the original lead, if you have one.

>
[Sustaining Steel](/Feats.aspx?ID=2874) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756), [inexorable iron hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=1)

**Trigger**
You Cast a Spell using a spell slot.

**Requirements**
You're in Arcane Cascade stance.

</column>

---

You pull magic into your weapon, using its substance to transform the magic into restorative energy. You regain Hit Points equal to double the spell's level and roll to end any [persistent negative damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) you have.

 If the spell was of the [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) school, any persistent negative damage you have ends automatically, and you can change the damage type from Arcane Cascade to positive if you wish. (Positive damage typically damages only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) or other creatures with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42).)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sustaining Steel](/Feats.aspx?ID=9079) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 23

**Prerequisites**
[inexorable iron hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=10)

**Trigger**
You [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) using a spell slot.

</column>

---

You pull magic from the surrounding area into your weapon, using its substance to transform the magic into restorative energy. You regain Hit Points equal to the triggering spell’s rank and roll to end any [persistent void damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) you have. If you’re in the [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) stance, the healing is equal to double the spell’s rank. 

If the spell had the [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) or [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) trait, any persistent vitality or void damage you have ends automatically, and you can change the damage type from Arcane Cascade to vitality or void if you wish. (Vitality damage typically damages only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or other creatures with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83).)

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 127 **Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807) --- You've learned how to use even your reflection to your advantage. You send your own reflection to forcibly swap places with the reflection of an enemy, pulling each of you through opposite ends and switching places. The enemy must be within 120 feet, you must both be adjacent to reflective surfaces (such as glass, mirrors, or calm water), and you must be able to see the target's reflection and have line of effect to it. The target attempts a Will save against your spell DC or class DC, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The spell has no effect.
**Success** You swap positions with your target or arrive adjacent to your target, whichever your target prefers.
**Failure** You swap positions with your target or arrive adjacent to your target, whichever you prefer.
**Critical Failure** You instantaneously swap positions with your target, and the target becomes trapped in its own reflection for 1 minute. Once on each of its turns, the target can spend 1 action to attempt another Will save to escape. If the save succeeds, the effect ends early.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swarmkeeper Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5463) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 72

**Archetype** [Swarmkeeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=223)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

Your body has become a symbiotic hive for a swarm of crawling insects. You can emit your swarm using the Swarm Forth action, and you can use the Bite and Sting action while your swarm is outside your body to command it to attack. Your deep connection to your swarm precludes you from also having an animal companion, though if an ability allows you to have more than one animal companion (such as the beastmaster archetype), you can count your swarm as one. You're immune to any damage from your swarm, and during your daily preparations you can anoint up to five willing creatures with a concoction made from your pheromones to grant them immunity as well.

 While outside your body, your swarm is Large and has a Speed of 15 feet and a climb Speed of 15 feet. It can occupy the same space as other creatures. While outside your body, the swarm can be attacked. It uses your statistics for defenses but is immune to [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that target only a specific number of creatures. The swarm has resistance equal to your level to physical damage and weakness equal to your level to area and splash damage. Any damage that would be dealt to the swarm is dealt to you instead, though you take damage only once from any ability that includes both you and the swarm in the area of effect (though you take the greater amount of damage).

 **Swarm Forth** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** Your swarm is within your body; **Effect** Your swarm boils forth from your body into a space adjacent to yours. (Its space can overlap yours.) It remains separate from you until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain the effect up to 1 minute. The effect also ends if you end your turn more than 60 feet away from the swarm. When you use Swarm Forth and each time you Sustain the effect, you can have the swarm Stride.

 When Swarm Forth ends, the swarm disperses into individual creatures. While dispersed, it can no longer be used for actions or be targeted, and the insects return to you and nest in your body again. This typically takes 1 minute unless you're extremely far away (as determined by the GM). 

**Bite and Sting** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Requirements** Your swarm is outside your body; **Effect** Each creature in your swarm's space takes 1d4 piercing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. At 4th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4.

<title level="2">Swarmkeeper Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aphet Flash](/Feats.aspx?ID=5464), [Buzzing Death Cicadas](/Feats.aspx?ID=5472), [Carried with the Swarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=5469), [Distracting Bites](/Feats.aspx?ID=5467), [Expanded Swarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=5473), [Mobile Swarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=5468), [Pyre Ant Sting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5465), [Sportlebore Choke](/Feats.aspx?ID=5470), [Veil of Bugs](/Feats.aspx?ID=5471), [Weaver's Web](/Feats.aspx?ID=5466)

If you were already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also become trained in swashbuckler class DC. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=527" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Fan Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=276)

**Prerequisites**
[Fan Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7039)

**Trigger**
You're targeted by a ranged attack that uses ammunition.

**Requirements**
You're wielding two fans, one in each hand.

</column>

---

You leap up on one leg, snapping your fans open alongside your head before sweeping them across your body. When you’re the target of an attack using ammunition (such as [arrows](/Weapons.aspx?ID=443), [bolts](/Weapons.aspx?ID=441), [sling bullets](/Weapons.aspx?ID=442), and other objects of similar size) while wielding two fans, whirl your fans to disrupt the incoming attack with gusts of air, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the triggering attack misses, you can redirect the ammunition into a nearby pocket or container where it can be retrieved and reused.

<title level="2">Sweeping Fan Block leads to...</title>
[Sweeping Fan Redirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7050)

You can redirect ammunition back at the creature that fired it with sweeping gusts of wind. You also apply any special effects the ammunition might have.

When danger appears, you quickly send away your active companion and call in a different animal ally. You use Call Companion.     level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swift Intervention](/Feats.aspx?ID=3120) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 50

**Archetype** [Overwatch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=109)

**Prerequisites**
[Overwatch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3118)

**Trigger**
An ally within your overwatch field fails in their attempt to [Arrest a Fall](/Actions.aspx?ID=91), [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28), [Grab a Ledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95), or [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=30).

**Requirements**
You are wielding a ranged weapon.

</column>

---

You're burdened with noticing potential threats at all times. Because of this, you've learned that a well-placed shot can prevent disaster. You make a shot to either pin an ally's clothing to stop a fall or secure them against a ledge, or you bounce an attack off their armor to correct their course as they stumble while attempting to balance or fly.

 Make a single ranged attack roll against the DC of the triggering check; your ally uses the result of your ranged attack roll in place of their original roll. You must have line of effect to your ally, and your attack roll includes any normal bonuses or penalties for a ranged attack with that weapon (such as the penalty for making a ranged attack beyond your first range increment).

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=811" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 99

**Prerequisites**
blessed swiftness

</column>

---

The movement of you and your allies is swift and decisive as the judgment of your deity. If your ally starts a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action in your champion's aura, their movement during that action doesn't trigger reactions. In addition, you're permanently [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89). You can use your extra action only to Step or Stride. If you have a fly Speed, add [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) to this list. If you have an animal companion and are mounted on it at the start of your turn, you can have your mount be quickened that turn instead of you.

Your keen eyes catch signs of passage even when you’re moving. You can move at your full Speed while you Track. If you have master proficiency in Survival, you don’t need to attempt a new Survival check every hour while Tracking. >
[Swim Through Earth](/Feats.aspx?ID=4230) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 27

</column>

---

The earth parts before you, letting you swim through it. You gain a burrow Speed equal to your land Speed and can immediately [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) once. You don't gain the ability to breathe while in the earth, so you must [hold your breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). The impulse ends at the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain it up to 1 minute. If you're inside the earth when the impulse ends, you immediately return to the surface directly above you, fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) when you reach the surface, and are [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until the end of your next turn.

---
**Level (14th)** You can burrow through rock and similar dense earthen matter, leaving no tunnels or signs of your passing.

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 18 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Add the [Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) trait to Swimming Charge._ **Requirements** You are swimming in water. --- You swim directly into a foe, attempting to push them out of the way. [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) up to your Speed, attempting to enter the space of a foe that’s your size or smaller. Roll an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check and compare the result of the Fortitude DC of the target creature. If the foe can’t move into an empty space (if it is surrounded by solid objects or other creatures, for example), you automatically critically fail this check. **Critical Success** The target takes bludgeoning damage equal to your level plus twice your Strength modifier and must move into the empty space directly behind it; you move into the space it vacated. The target must move even if doing so places it in harm’s way.
**Success** As critical success, but the damage is equal to your level plus your Strength modifier.
**Failure** The target takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier and you end your movement before entering its space.
**Critical Failure** The target is unaffected and you end your movement before entering its space.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 111

**Archetypes** [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120) (Level 4), [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=367) (Level 4)

</column>

---

You're comfortable wielding a firearm or crossbow in one hand and a melee weapon in the other, combining melee attacks with shots from the firearm. When you make a successful ranged Strike against an enemy within your reach with your one-handed firearm or one-handed crossbow, that enemy is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against your next melee attack with a one-handed melee weapon.

 When you make a successful melee Strike against an enemy with your one-handed melee weapon, the next ranged Strike you make against that enemy with a one-handed firearm or one-handed crossbow doesn't trigger reactions that would trigger on a ranged attack but not a melee attack, such as [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256). Either of these benefits is lost if not used by the end of your next turn.

Your spiritual power pierces both body and soul, pinning your foe in place. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a one-handed, [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), or [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) weapon, or your fist unarmed attack. The target can end this immobilization with a successful [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) attempt using the higher of your class DC or your spell DC as the Escape DC.

    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 55

**Archetype** [Aldori Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=324)

**Prerequisites**
[Aldori Duelist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7899); you have broken or forsaken the Aldori swordpact.

</column>

---

You are a swordlord exile. You have abandoned or been abandoned by the Aldori Academy. Aldori swordlords are honor-bound to challenge you on sight. Additionally, your unbridled skill strikes terror in those around you. You can use Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) instead of Intimidation to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) and [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) while your [Aldori dueling sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535) is visible to the target of your attempt. 

With broken pride, your blade is now a disgraced tool used to remove obstacles between you and your goals, whatever they may be. The first time you hit a creature with an Aldori dueling sword each round, you deal 5 additional precision damage.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Aldori Swordlord](/Feats.aspx?ID=7911).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Kitharodian Actor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=301)

**Prerequisites**
[Kitharodian Actor Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7456)

</column>

---

You portrayed Grand Prince Stavian III in _Fall of the Troubled King_, a production dedicated to the life and times of the paranoid Taldan ruler whose violent resistance to new policies on succession kicked off the War for the Crown. Your acting won rave reviews for recasting Stavian’s paranoia and political machinations in a sympathetic light, and you’ve learned to apply these subtle techniques outside of the stage to win others over. Whenever you succeed at a Deception or Performance check to portray a famous figure, you can select one creature within 60 feet who observed your performance. As long as this creature isn’t hostile, its attitude toward you automatically improves by two steps (three steps if your check was a critical success). If it’s hostile, it’s [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2 for 1 minute as it tries to reconcile its desire to harm you with its newfound sympathy for you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sympathetic Vulnerabilities](/Feats.aspx?ID=3714) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227), mortal weakness or personal antithesis

</column>

---

When you apply your will to invoke a vulnerability, the result is more powerful, and the vulnerability ripples out in a web from your main target to affect a broader range of creatures. This has one of two effects, based on the type of vulnerability you invoked.

 While you have mortal weakness applied, your Strikes also apply that weakness against any creature that has that weakness, not just creatures of the exact same kind. For instance, if you used mortal weakness against a [red dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=168) to apply its weakness to cold to your Strikes, those Strikes would also apply to the weakness to cold of [fire elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=43) or any other creature with a weakness to cold.

 While you have personal antithesis applied to a non-[humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) creature, you can apply your custom weakness to all creatures of the exact same kind. For example, if you used personal antithesis against an [imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=109), the custom weakness would apply to other imps but not to other non-imp [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30).

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Syncretism](/Feats.aspx?ID=1186) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 105

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Remove the final sentence of Syncretism that specifies the feat’s benefit if your cleric doctrine is not cloistered cleric or warpriest._

**Prerequisites**
you follow a deity

</column>

---

You have come to see the overlap between two deities’ teachings. Choose a second deity. You must meet their alignment requirements, and you are subject to their edicts and anathema. If you are a cloistered cleric, select one of that deity’s domains, gaining the benefits of the [Expanded Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=1172) feat with that domain. If you are a warpriest, you gain the favored weapon of that deity as a second favored weapon, and it gains the benefits of feats and abilities you have that affect your deity’s favored weapon, such as [Deadly Simplicity](/Feats.aspx?ID=264). If you have a different doctrine than cloistered cleric or warpriest, either apply whichever of the above options is most appropriate for your doctrine, or, at the GM’s discretion, add a benefit from the second deity more closely tied to your doctrine.

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Living Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=1570)

</column>

---

Your hair unarmed attack deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage and gains the [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) trait.

<title level="2">Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 74

The player characters might learn some of these techniques from friends and rivals during their stay on Bonmu, allowing them to select the feats the next time they would gain a feat. You can expertly control your living hair and use it to perform various tasks. You can perform simple Interact actions with your hair such as opening an unlocked door or picking up objects. Your hair can't perform actions that require fingers or significant manual dexterity, including any action that would require a check to accomplish. Your hair can hold items of up to 1 Bulk, but can't Activate or attack with any items it's holding.

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 232

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41)

</column>

---

Even if you don’t know much about its constituent creatures, you can always recognize a troop’s capabilities through features like the formation they move in or even more subtle hints others might miss. You can always use [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) when you [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) to identify a troop. This works like using an applicable Lore to identify a creature. If you’re legendary in Warfare Lore, reduce any adjustment to the Recall Knowledge check’s DC caused by the troop’s rarity by 5.

If you [lead a troop](/Rules.aspx?ID=3439), when you successfully use Warfare Lore to identify a troop, that troop takes a –1 circumstance penalty to saves against your troop’s offensive abilities until the end of your next turn.

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tag Team](/Feats.aspx?ID=3264) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121)

**Prerequisites**
[Sniping Duo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3258)

**Trigger**
You or your spotter misses with a Strike against a creature, and the creature is within the other's melee reach or first range increment.

</column>

---

Your skilled teamwork with your spotter enables you both to assist one another when you falter, using either other's failures as opportunities to strike. If you used Tag Team after your spotter missed the triggering Strike, make a ranged Strike against the same target with a –2 penalty. If you used this reaction after you missed the triggering Strike, your spotter can use their reaction to make a melee or ranged Strike against the same target. Strikes granted by this feat don't count toward your or your spotter's multiple attack penalty and your or your spotter's multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to the granted Strike.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Talisman Dabbler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2079) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 195

**Archetype** [Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=79)

</column>

---

You are trained in the use of [talismans](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=19) and similar magical paraphernalia. This training might have occurred in a formal classroom or been an agglomeration of folk magic picked up over time. You can craft talismans and know the formulas for all common talismans in the _Core Rulebook_ of your level or lower. You remember talisman formulas and don't need a [formula book](/Equipment.aspx?ID=22) for them.

 Additionally, you carry a collection of magical baubles you can turn into temporary talismans. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each talisman's formula. A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it.

 Finally, when you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=520), you can (in any combination) affix or remove up to four talismans in the 10-minute span.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the talisman dabbler archetype.

<title level="2">Talisman Dabbler Dedication leads to...</title>
[Deeper Dabbler](/Feats.aspx?ID=2081), [Quick Fix](/Feats.aspx?ID=2080), [Talismanic Sage](/Feats.aspx?ID=2082)

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 51

**Archetype** [Eagle Knight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314)

once per day

    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Talon's Mark](/Feats.aspx?ID=8859) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 36

**Archetype** [Twilight Talon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=375)

**Prerequisites**
[Twilight Talon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8858)

**Requirements**
You have a magical or mundane tattoo.

</column>

---

On the rare occasions that Twilight Talons need to identify themselves as members of the organization, many rely on an easily concealed tattoo to reveal their allegiance. Choose a tattoo you have. If the tattoo wasn't already a magic item, it becomes a level 6 item with the [invested](/Traits.aspx?ID=637), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), and [tattoo](/Traits.aspx?ID=262) traits. It also gains the following abilities.

 **Activate—Twist Design** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) You transform your tattoo to a different form of approximately the same size. You can Dismiss this effect.

 **Activate—Adopt Persona** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) Frequency once per day; Effect Your tattoo helps you create a temporary cover to infiltrate a protected area or escape a dangerous situation. It casts 2nd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) and 2nd-rank [_ventriloquism_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1740) on you. The duration of both effects is 10 minutes.

<title level="2">Talon's Mark leads to...</title>
[Inked Cache](/Feats.aspx?ID=8864), [Instant Credentials](/Feats.aspx?ID=8866)

fields.markdown:
May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame **Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) --- Animals born and raised far from humanoid settlements rarely get along with two-legged beings, whom they assume to be dangerous predators. In spite of this, you know how to approach and entreat a wild animal so that it's more receptive to your presence and requests. To use this feat, choose a wild [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) that isn't actively hostile to you and which isn't confined to an area smaller than its Speed in diameter (animals held in place or trapped are typically too scared to be tamed). Attempt a Nature check against a DC determined by the GM; this is usually the animal's Will DC, but circumstances might adjust the precise DC. This attempt usually takes an hour, but you can perform it in 10 minutes if you have expert proficiency in Nature, 1 minute if you have master proficiency, or as a three-action activity if you have legendary proficiency. **Critical Success** You form a friendly bond with the animal. As long as it isn't starving, the animal won't attack you or creatures obviously allied with you, even if they're creatures the animal would normally prey upon. This effect is permanent.
**Success** As critical success, but the effect lasts for 1 month. If you or an ally teach the animal a basic action during that time with the [Train Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=856) skill feat, the effect is permanent.
**Failure** You fail to make any kind of meaningful impression on the animal.
**Critical Failure** The animal does its best to attack you and is immune to Tame Animal for 1 month. Skill Feats **Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78 Characters can gain access to the following new skill feats throughout “Broken Tusk Moon.” **All of the Animal**: Head scout Wipa teaches this skill feat to characters who help her butcher an animal for meat, such as the moose at the beginning of the adventure or another animal slain throughout the course of the Broken Tusk following's journey. **Spirit Speaker**: Mammoth Lord Argakoa, also known as Argakoa the Songsinger, might teach a fraction of her tremendous skill to a young scout who joins her in song. **Tame Animal**: The young herd tender Imek has a natural way with animals. She is happy to teach what she knows to any characters who display a similar reverence toward living creatures, such as by peacefully resolving their encounter with the giant porcupine in Chapter 1 of this adventure. Although this feat is particularly useful to characters who want to recruit animal followers throughout the Quest for the Frozen Flame Adventure Path, it isn't strictly necessary for the party to succeed in their adventures. It can be a great boon to parties taking part in other quests, as well. **Related Feats**: [All of the Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3422), [Spirit Speaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3423)

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 25 --- You tamper with a foe's weapon or armor, using a free hand. Choose either a weapon held by an enemy in your reach or a suit of armor worn by an enemy in your reach. Attempt a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check against the enemy's Reflex DC. **Critical Success** Your tampering is incredibly effective. If you tampered with a weapon, the enemy takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and damage rolls with that weapon. If you tampered with armor, the armor hampers the enemy's movement, making the enemy flat-footed and inflicting a –10-foot penalty to its Speeds. The effect lasts until the enemy Interacts to remove it, regardless of which one you used.
**Success** Your tampering is temporarily effective. As critical success, but the effect ends at the start of your next turn, even if the enemy doesn't Interact to end it.
**Critical Failure** Your tampering backfires dramatically, creating a small explosion from your own tools or gear. You take fire damage equal to your level.

You extend your arms like gnarled branches to interfere with your foes’ movements. You can make lashing branch unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, finesse, nonlethal, and unarmed traits.

 While you’re in Tangled Forest Stance and can act, every enemy in your reach that tries to move away from you must succeed at a Reflex save, Acrobatics check, or Athletics check against your class DC or be immobilized for that action. If you prefer, you can allow the enemy to move.

<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 140

**Prerequisites**
[Living Vessel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3815)

</column>

---

You tap into the entity's life force to heal your wounds, though at the cost of the entity's personality bleeding into your own. You recover a number of Hit Points equal to four times your level. Each time you use Tap Vitality, you begin to bleed more and more of the entity's personality and instincts into your own until the next time you spend an hour or more assuaging the entity, bringing your mind back under your own control.

**Special** This action has the tradition trait appropriate to your entity, typically [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) for a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) for an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) or outer entity, or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134) for a [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69)

**Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=66)

**Prerequisites**
[Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2005)

**Trigger**
An ally succeeds at a ranged Strike against an opponent within your weapon's first range increment.

**Requirements**
You have a ranged or [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapon in hand.

</column>

---

You capitalize on your ally's attack to create a coordinated barrage. Make a ranged Strike with a –2 penalty against the opponent targeted by the triggering attack. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike. If this Strike is successful, combine the damage from the attack with the damage from your ally's attack for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.

[Target of Psychic Ire](/Feats.aspx?ID=3689) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Amp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=425" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 29

</column>

---

Your magic saturates your surroundings with hateful psychic energy. Use this amp in place of a psi cantrip's normal amp entry. The cantrip must be one that takes 2 or more actions to cast and targets a creature.

---
**Amp** Choose one target of the spell. Psychic phenomena turn themselves on the target—typically, objects fling themselves at the creature. At the beginning of each of the target's turns, it takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage for each spell level of the psi cantrip this amp was added to, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The target remains marked by psychic ire for 3 rounds. The effect persists even if you fall unconscious or leave the area.

>
[Targeted Redirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=3261) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 137

**Archetype** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121)

**Prerequisites**
[Sniping Duo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3258)

</column>

---

You aim a shot at your spotter, intending for your spotter to redirect that shot off their own weapon or shield to hit your foe from a better angle, and avoid your foe's cover. If your next action is to make a ranged Strike, you treat your spotter's position as your own for the purposes of determining cover and range. Your spotter must be within your weapon's first range increment and they must use a reaction to redirect your shot.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 92 --- Your attack harms and hinders your foe. Choose a particular part of your foe from the list below and Strike. If you hit and damage the target, apply the effect corresponding to the chosen part. This hindrance lasts until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, you also apply a lesser effect lasting for 1 minute.
  • **Arm (or another limb used for attacks, such as a tentacle)** The target is [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13). On a critical hit, it is also enfeebled 1 for 1 minute.
  • **Head** The target is [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). On a critical hit, it is also stupefied 1 for 1 minute.
  • **Legs** The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds. On a critical hit, it also takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Taste Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=2349) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Dhampir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=215" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 27

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) As specified in the feat, a PC who uses this feat on an unwilling target that is not an active combatant commits an evil act; in Pathfinder Society play, doing so earns the PC 1 Point of Infamy._

**Prerequisites**
[Cel Rau](/Feats.aspx?ID=2343), [Straveika](/Feats.aspx?ID=1337), [Svetocher](/Feats.aspx?ID=1338), or another lineage from a vampire with the Drink Blood ability

</column>

---

You retain not only your vampiric parent's taste for blood but their ability to gain vitality from it. You drink fresh blood from a living [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) creature, gaining temporary Hit Points equal to the target's level that last for 10 minutes. The target must succeed at a Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC or become [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). Regardless of the outcome of this save, the target is temporarily immune to your Taste Blood for 1 day; further uses of this ability against the target don't increase the drained condition or grant you more temporary Hit Points.

 To drink a creature's blood, either your last action must have been a fangs Strike that damaged the target, or the target must be restrained or unconscious and your last action must have been a Strike that dealt piercing or slashing damage to them. If the target is willing, they don't need to be restrained or unconscious for the latter. 

Draining the life force from an unwilling humanoid creature is a greater violation than just drinking their blood. Taste Blood has the [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64) trait unless the target is willing or is an active foe in combat.

You become trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45); if you are already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain access to all uncommon [magical tattoos](/Rules.aspx?ID=1495) with the [orc](/Traits.aspx?ID=666) trait.

You gain a [_storied skin_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3658) for free upon gaining this feat (or another magical tattoo of 2nd level or lower if you already have _storied skin_). You cannot have more than one _storied skin_ tattoo, but the frequency of its Living History ability increases by one use per minute for every three tattooed historian feats you have. For every two tattooed historian feats you have, you can [invest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2619) one magical tattoo that does not count against the maximum number of items you can have invested at one time.

Your shapeshifting is advanced enough to take the form of not just creatures, but objects as well. When you Change Shape, you can assume the form of a simple tool or object of 1 Bulk or less, such as a teakettle or umbrella. When transformed into an object, you can function as that object for allies to use; for instance, turning into a crowbar so you can help an ally pry open a crate. You can speak while in object form, but you can’t attack, cast spells, or move except to [Crawl](/Actions.aspx?ID=2293) (usually by hopping or flopping across the ground in an undignified manner).

<title level="2">Teakettle Form leads to...</title>

A thin shell of telekinetic energy pushes from your skin, widening your enemy's grasp enough for you to slip free. You gain a +2 status bonus to checks to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) from whatever has you grabbed or restrained. This bonus lasts until either you're no longer grabbed or restrained, or you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38).

Your union is so strong, you can communicate with each other without uttering a word, even across vast distances. You and your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) can communicate telepathically while within 1 mile of each other as if you were speaking your shared language. You and your companion can also sense each other’s general emotions as long as you are on the same plane, allowing you to know if the other is in peril or under great distress.

[Telling Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=8163) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

Your determination empowers a telling blow to defeat your most powerful enemies. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). Make a Strike at mythic proficiency. If the Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. You can spend additional Mythic Points after determining the outcome of the attack to deal one more die of weapon damage per extra Mythic Point spent. If the target of your attack is your nemesis or an ally of your nemesis, you gain two die of weapon damage per extra Mythic Point spent.

If you have no Mythic Points remaining after using this ability, you gain the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) condition.

Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42), or Herbalism Lore

**Access**

</column>

---

You learn Hwan temperature classifications for the elements—wood and water are cold elements, while fire, earth, and metal are hot elements. When you [Prepare Elemental Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=7065), you can alter the environmental effects on the recipient’s body. If you created hot elemental medicine, the recipient ignores the effects of severe cold while the medicine lasts. If you created cold elemental medicine, the recipient ignores the effects of severe heat while the medicine lasts.

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Temporal Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=8171) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 82

**Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340)

**Prerequisites**
[Timewracked Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8166)

</column>

---

You shift and skip through time, vanishing during your movement to appear in unexpected and advantageous locations for combat. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). Strike, then Step up to 10 feet. This movement is affected normally by barriers and [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366); you still move physically through the area, just so swiftly that it appears that you’ve teleported. Then, make another Strike. Apply your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289) to both Strikes normally, but this second Strike is made at mythic proficiency and your target is [off guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against it.

<title level="2">Temporal Fury leads to...</title>
[Echoing Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=8173)

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Temporary Potions](/Feats.aspx?ID=1580) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 103

**Prerequisites**
[Cauldron](/Feats.aspx?ID=1562)

</column>

---

During your daily preparations, you can create a batch of two temporary [oils](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=17) or [potions](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=18) using a formula you know. These items follow the normal rules to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) them, except for the time they take, with some additional restrictions. They must both be the same type of oil or potion, and their level must be 6 or more levels lower than your level. Any items you create this way become inert bottles of liquid the next time you make your daily preparations, and any remaining effects of the temporary items end. A temporary oil or potion has no value.

 If you have master proficiency in your tradition's spell DCs, you can create a batch of three temporary oils or potions during your daily preparations, and if you have legendary proficiency, you can create a batch of four.

Your gentle magic eases even the most skittish of souls, a gift that almost guarantees you popularity among parents and farmers alike. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tengu Feather Fan](/Feats.aspx?ID=2439) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tengu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=240" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 58

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The fan you gain from this feat is a held item._

</column>

---

You've learned to bind some of your feathers together into a fan to focus your ancestral magic. You gain a _tengu feather fan_: a magic item of light Bulk with a level equal to your level and the [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65) and [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134) traits. You (and only you) can use the _tengu feather fan_ to cast tengu magic. If your fan is lost or destroyed, you can create a replacement during your daily preparations; if you do so, your previous fan falls apart into mundane feathers. Further feats might grant you additional activations of your _tengu feather fan_, but you can never have more than three activations per day, no matter how many such feats you have. The DC for spells you cast with your _tengu feather fan_ is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

 You can cast the 1st-level [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) spell by activating your tengu feather fan.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast one of the spells contained in your _tengu feather fan_. Activating the fan takes the spell's normal number of actions. You can also Activate the fan to cast a cantrip you've gained from a heritage or ancestry feat; this activation doesn't count against the fan's uses per day

<title level="2">Tengu Feather Fan leads to...</title>
[Wind God's Fan](/Feats.aspx?ID=2440)

You (and only you) can cast tengu magic with the Wave Fan activation.
