You can instead cast a cantrip you've gained from a heritage or an ancestry feat; this doesn't use up one of the fan's daily activations.

 This activation takes the spell's normal number of actions. The spell's DC is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

You've trained with a blade and other tengu weapons ever since you hatched. You gain access to [khakkaras](/Weapons.aspx?ID=126). Additionally, choose two weapons from the [sword](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15) group. You can choose from among all common martial swords, plus the [katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=55), [temple sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=61), and [wakizashi](/Weapons.aspx?ID=129). For the purpose of determining your proficiency, that weapon is a simple weapon, and if the weapon isn't common, you gain access to it. If you are trained in all martial weapons, you add common advanced swords to the swords you can choose from.

 You also gain access to all uncommon tengu weapons. For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial tengu weapons are simple weapons, and advanced tengu weapons are martial weapons.

You often find that the best way to win a conflict means avoiding a fight in the first place. You're good at talking to potential opponents without making things worse. **Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 141

---

You capture transformative fragments of magic and slam them into the ground, creating a shock wave that alters your surroundings. If your next action is to Cast a non-cantrip transmutation Spell, either each space adjacent to you becomes difficult terrain, or each space adjacent to you is no longer difficult terrain. This doesn't have any effect on greater difficult terrain and doesn't remove the damaging effects of hazardous terrain.

Your experience in navigating a certain type of terrain makes you supremely confident while doing so. **Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different type of terrain each time.

A Strike would damage you.

**Requirements**
You gained a terrain attunement benefit since the start of your most recent turn and that attunement matches the terrain you're in.

</column>

---

You're so attuned to the land that it rises up to protect you from a potentially fatal blow in a seeming coincidence. For instance, a branch suddenly falls from a nearby tree to take the brunt of a sword swing or a surprising change of current disrupts an enemy's attack. You gain resistance to physical damage equal to double your level against the triggering Strike.

[Terrain Stalker](/Feats.aspx?ID=5224) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 263

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

Select one type of difficult terrain from the following list: rubble, snow, or underbrush. While undetected by all non-allies in that type of terrain, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than 5 feet and do not pass within 10 feet of an enemy during your movement.

During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren’t actively Searching or on guard.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different type of terrain.

Your Elemental Assault cycles through all four elements. When you use Elemental Assault, instead of choosing a single element, you can choose an element from the list when using the action, and then choose a different element at the beginning of each of your next 3 turns without spending an action; once you have chosen an element, you can't choose it again during this Elemental Assault, meaning you must select all four elements over the course of 4 turns. Each time you choose an element, until the beginning of your next turn, your Strikes deal an additional 1d6 damage of the indicated type and have the trait corresponding to that element.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[That's Not Natural!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3897) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 9

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

Your mastery at surviving in the wild has given you a sort of sixth-sense when it comes to noticing creatures that aren't part of the natural order. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all initiative checks made at the start of a battle in which at least one of your enemies is an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69), [mutant](/Traits.aspx?ID=229), or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), or if one of your enemies is from a plane other than the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1), as long as the battle takes place in a wilderness region. In wilderness regions, you also increase your Perception DC by 1 against these types of creatures for the purposes of resolving their [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks. If you're master in Survival, this circumstance bonus increases to +2.

 If you know the [_commune with nature_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=7) ritual, you can use Survival as a primary or secondary check to resolve that ritual—if you do so, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus.

<title level="2">Adventuring with Amiri</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 8

As Amiri explores the Stolen Lands, her legend grows with her. Already a larger-than-life personality, she begins to accidentally encourage something akin to a cult of personality in the PCs' kingdom. If brought to her attention that a new generation of adventurers are using her exploits and legends as an inspiration for their own adventuring style, she's amused but also perhaps a bit put off by the idea.

 The following new skill feats become available to the PCs starting at 4th level, assuming Amiri remains allied with them.

**Related Feats**: [Say that Again!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3898), [Too Angry to Die](/Feats.aspx?ID=3899), [Triumphant Boast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3896)

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[That's Odd](/Feats.aspx?ID=1449) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 60

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) GMs should provide a character with the That’s Odd investigator feat a hint whenever the character enters a room with hidden aspects, specifically with regard to hidden passageways (such as scuff marks near a bookcase that’s actually a swinging door), creatures or hazards (such as drippage on the floor from an unseen fungus growing on the rafters), or valuables (such as bunched carpet over a secret compartment in the floor that contains a bag of coins). The GM does not need to provide clues for rooms that have no significant secret or hidden features. These clues should indicate only that the character should investigate a given section of the room, not let them automatically uncover the hidden element or provide any additional information beyond signaling its presence._

</column>

---

When you enter a new location, such as a room or corridor, you immediately notice one thing out of the ordinary. The GM determines what it is, or whether there's nothing reasonable to pick up, skipping obvious clues that can be easily noticed without a check or specifically looking for them. You learn only that an area or object is suspicious, but not why it's suspicious. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 49

**Archetype** [Thaumaturge](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=186)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14

</column>

---

You've uncovered basic thaumaturgy. You become trained in thaumaturge class DC. Choose an [implement](/Implements.aspx); you can use it to Glimpse Vulnerability, but don't gain its benefits. You also gain a few esoterica, allowing you to use [esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=427) actions. You become trained in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); if you were already trained in these, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the Glimpse Vulnerability action.

 **Glimpse Vulnerability** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=427), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)); **Frequency** once per round; **Requirement** You are holding your implement; **Effect** You glimpse a hidden vulnerability and then strengthen it to aid you. Select a creature you can see. Until you Glimpse Vulnerability again, that target gains weakness 2 against your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) and weapon Strikes.

<title level="2">Thaumaturge Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Thaumaturgy](/Feats.aspx?ID=3744), [Implement Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=3746), [Magical Knowledge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3747), [Resolute](/Feats.aspx?ID=3748)

[Thaumaturge's Demesne](/Feats.aspx?ID=3723) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 46

</column>

---

You have claimed an area or location as your demesne, granting you the ability to ward and protect it. When you select this feat, choose a demesne, an area of no more than 2,000 square feet. You must legitimately own the area or, if its a public area, you must lay claim to the area without anyone contesting it.

 Once you've chosen your demesne, it's automatically protected by an arcane [_private sanctum_](/Spells.aspx?ID=235) spell with an unlimited duration, heightened to half your level rounded up and using your thaumaturge class DC in place of a spell DC, if necessary. Additionally, the demesne is attended by three unseen custodians, as a successful [_unseen custodians_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=39) ritual, and one object in the area gains an elemental sentinel, as a successful [_elemental sentinel_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=57) ritual.

<title level="2">Thaumaturge's Demesne leads to...</title>
[Unlimited Demesne](/Feats.aspx?ID=3734)

---

Your studies into the supernatural have resulted in an especially strong knowledge of [rituals](/Rules.aspx?ID=777). You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all primary checks to perform a ritual. You learn two [uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=159) [rituals](/Rituals.aspx) with a level no higher than half your level; you must meet all prerequisites for casting the ritual to choose it. You can cast these as the primary caster, but you can't teach them to anyone else or allow someone else to serve as primary caster unless they know the ritual as well.

 At 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you learn another uncommon ritual with a level no higher than half your level and for which you meet the prerequisites.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 115

**Archetype** [Cultivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=278)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghost-path Epiphany](/Feats.aspx?ID=7091)

</column>

---

Tian Xia’s shining cities belie its empires’ long shadow of death, darkened by thousands of years of suffering and injustice. You pursue immortality not through tuft-hunting with Heaven’s dragons or their imperial brats; yours is the power to crack its corrupt wheel, for you can now release the ghost gates to expedite the dead’s revenge at being cheated of their fates. 

You cease aging and, regardless of your actual existential state, now register as an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) to effects that can detect undead (such as [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) or spiritsense). In addition, you learn [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=117) rituals for [gashadokuro](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1860), [jiangshi](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=286), and [shui gui](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2784). On a success with one of these rituals, you gain the effects of a critical success instead.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
You are reduced to 0 Hit Points and would gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition or would otherwise die.

</column>

---

Death is as natural as breathing to you, and you can move past it as easily as the other troubles in your life. You prevent yourself from [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) and regain Hit Points equal to 6d8 plus half your level. If the cause of your death was a condition or effect that would still cause you to die after regaining Hit Points, such as a high value on the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition, you suppress that effect for 1 minute.

---

You beseech warrior spirits to come forth and aid you. Two ghostly warriors manifest within a 30-foot emanation of you and each attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against an adjacent enemy, using your spell attack modifier. The warriors' Strikes each deal 4d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage and the warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies. If you are [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) 2 when you use The Dead Walk, you instead summon three warriors, and if you are cursebound 3, you instead summon four warriors. The warriors disappear at the start of your next turn.

</column>

---

You know how to make a larger creature hurt when it falls to the ground. If you successfully [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) a foe that's larger than you, it takes 1d8 bludgeoning damage (or 2d8 bludgeoning damage on a critical success). If you are master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), the damage increases to 2d8 bludgeoning (or 4d8 bludgeoning on a critical success).

<title level="2">Adventuring with Ekundayo</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23

Ekundayo eventually develops his own methods to pursue his favored enemies—giants. Once he gains the Magical Crafting feat at 4th level, he begins to craft specialized ammunition and runes for weapons. As long as his attitude toward the PCs is at least friendly, he shares these discoveries with them, unlocking the following ranger class feats and items as soon as his level equals the level of the feat or item.

**Related Feats**: [Giant Hunter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3900), [Giant Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3904), [Hamstringing Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3902), [Roll with It (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3903)

fields.text: Feat 16 The Immortal Attains the Summit Archetype Source Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 115 Archetype Cultivator Prerequisites Three Pecks of Dew Your cultivation bearing glorious fruit, you behold Heaven’s will. Returning from your vision of the Holy Mountain, you become an immortal with mystic potency over the terrestrial realms of wind and water. You cease aging and, regardless of your actual existential state, now register as a living being to effects that can detect living creatures (such as lifesense or spiritsense). In addition, you learn the control weather and plant growth rituals. You can use Occultism instead of Nature for these rituals. On a success with one of these rituals, you gain the effects of a critical success instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[The Shattered Mountain Weeps](/Feats.aspx?ID=4235) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 27

</column>

---

A massive sphere of rock explodes, unleashing a cataclysm of falling debris and deadly shrapnel. Its destruction falls in a 20-foot burst within 120 feet. Creatures in the area take 9d10 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC. Those who fail are knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). For the next minute, rocks continue to fall, making the area [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage to any creature that ends its turn in the area. If you use this impulse again, any previous one ends.

---
**Level (20th)** The initial damage is 10d10, and the area damage is 4d10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[The Thousand Lashes of the Weeping Willow](/Feats.aspx?ID=7625) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 73

</column>

---

You conjure a massive willow tree, which lashes your foes with a thousand branches. The trunk of the weeping willow tree is 10-feet in diameter and appears in an unoccupied space within 500 feet. The tree whips its branches at all your enemies within a 30-foot-radius [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) centered on the willow’s trunk, dealing 10d8 slashing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that fails its save is also overcome with sorrow, becoming [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for as long as the willow remains, as it weeps uncontrollably. The willow doesn’t target you or your allies.

The willow tree remains until the end of your next turn, but you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) it up to 1 minute. The first time you Sustain the impulse each round, the weeping willow attacks again, dealing 4d8 slashing damage to all enemies in the area with a basic reflex save. If you use this impulse again, the previous one ends.

---
**Level (20th)** The initial damage is 14d8, and the Sustained damage is 5d8.

fields.feat_markdown: The Truth as I See it
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 58 **Archetype** [Field Propagandist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=326) **Prerequisites** [Field Propagandist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7922) --- Your knack for spinning a believable reality from threads of story is so practiced that sometimes even you begin to believe what you're saying. When you use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to Lie, you can carefully structure your deceits so that each individual statement you make is the truth, from a certain perspective. Once per day when using Deception to Lie, you can roll twice and take the better result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.

You don't take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the [_ring of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1656) spell or similar effects. Whenever you are subject to _ring of truth_ or a similar effect, you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) the spell's effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up); succeeding at this check doesn't end the spell or effect, but it does cause it to indicate that you are speaking the truth, even when you are actually lying.

The oath's power is overwhelming—too much for a mortal frame—but victory is worth any price. When you use this feat, you cry out the final line of the Crimson Oath, unleashing unbridled power for 1 minute. You can Dismiss this effect. While this effect is active, you gain the following effects:
  • At the beginning of each of your turns, you become [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) or increase the value of your drained condition by 1 if you are already drained. You can't reduce the value of your drained condition or remove it while The Tyrant Falls! is active. While The Tyrant Falls! is active, your drained condition does not penalize your Fortitude save.
  • You can cast [_invoke the Crimson Oath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=556) at will without expending Focus Points. When you do, increase the area to a 40-foot cone.
  • You gain resistance to all damage equal to half your character level.
  • Any melee weapon you wield gains the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) trait if it didn't already possess it, or increases its reach by 5 feet if it already has the reach trait. Your Strikes with that weapon deal an extra 2d6 positive or negative damage (whichever is more effective against the target).

The creature must be Medium or smaller; if your waking world is a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), the creature can be Large or smaller, or Huge or smaller if your waking world is a 30-foot burst or larger. While devoured, it becomes grabbed and [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1, and takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns, and cannot be targeted by any effect. A creature can attempt to Escape against your world rouser DC; in addition to the normal checks to Escape, it can attempt a [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85) check. If it Escapes, it is returned to the area where it was when grabbed. A creature with a [burrow Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2348) can Escape automatically and move up to its burrow Speed as part of that action.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=80" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 32

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
You succeed at a skill check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) to identify a creature.

</column>

---

You study a creature’s form and behavior to hypothesize likely means of overcoming its strengths. Once before the end of your next turn, you can use the skill modifier from the triggering check in place of your saving throw modifier against one of the creature’s abilities, in place of your Perception modifier to Seek the creature, in place of your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) modifier to Feint against the creature, or in place of your [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) modifier to Demoralize the creature. Alternatively, against one of the creature’s attacks, you can use your DC for the skill used in the triggering check in place of your AC.

You direct waves of warmth into or out of your kinetic gate to drastically shift the temperature around you. Choose cold or fire. **Archetypes** [Druid](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=6), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) (Level 20), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=218) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Your mask grants you the toughness of Elephant, the Conjured Chronicle. Increase your maximum number of Hit Points by 20. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only you, you gain resistance 10 to all physical damage until the start of your next turn.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[This is What It's Like to Die](/Feats.aspx?ID=8216) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Reincarnated" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=903" />
<trait label="Universal Ancestry" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=467" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Season of Ghosts (Hardcover)](/Sources.aspx?ID=294) pg. 321

</column>

---

It’s one thing to remember your previous lives. It’s quite another to remember how you died in each of those lives. You can recall dozens, if not more, of excruciating, humiliating, and devastating ends you’ve suffered over the eons, and you can inflict upon your enemies a vision of these pains. You gain [_phantasmagoria_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1629) as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) that you can cast once per day. When you gain this feat, choose any two of the following damage types: [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), bludgeoning, [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), piercing, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), slashing, or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697). These damage types caused your deaths more often than not in your previous lives, and whenever a creature takes damage from a _phantasmagoria_ spell you cast, you can swap the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage that spell normally causes for one of the two damage types you chose.

>
[Thlipit Contestant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5474) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Thlipit Contestant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=224)

**Prerequisites**
You have a long prehensile tongue or a tail. At the GM’s discretion, similar flexible appendages, such as tentacles, can be used to qualify instead.

</column>

---

Grueling practice has strengthened your tongue or tail to the point where it's become a formidable weapon. You gain a lash melee [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack that is in the [flail](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=7) weapon group, deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage, and has the [grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) and [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) traits. The attack can be performed with any appendages you used to qualify for this feat.

<title level="2">Thlipit Contestant Dedication leads to...</title>

---

Your devotion to the ideals of justice, freedom, and revolution allow you to truly punish those who stand in your way. When you critically succeed at a Hellbreaker Strike, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or become [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1 (stunned 2 on a critical failure). This effect has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

You take your time searching to ensure you find everything. When [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519), you can take twice as long to search. <traits>
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 25

</column>

---

You can create a prototypical creature from the depths of your imagination instead of calling one from elsewhere. Whenever you summon a creature, you can choose to instead create a psychic construct of that creature. This grants it resistance to physical damage equal to half its level, weakness 5 to force and mental damage, and the ability to pass through enemies' spaces without needing to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) (though it can't end its turn in an occupied space).

    pfs="Standard"

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

You can detect the flickers of mental activity let off by all thinking creatures. You gain thoughtsense as a [vague](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) sense that has a range of 30 feet—like all vague senses, it's only about as precise as an average human's sense of smell, meaning you generally can predict only if a creature is present. Your thoughtsense detects only thinking creatures, so a creature that is unthinking or otherwise immune to mental effects (such as many constructs and oozes) can't be perceived using your thoughtsense, regardless of how precise it is. 

While your [Psyche is Unleashed](/Actions.aspx?ID=1222), your thoughtsense upgrades to an imprecise [sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=412), letting you use it to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) out creatures.

fields.text: Feat 8 Thoughtsense Mental Psychic Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 27 You can detect the flickers of mental activity let off by all thinking creatures. You gain thoughtsense as a vague sense that has a range of 30 feet—like all vague senses, it's only about as precise as an average human's sense of smell, meaning you generally can predict only if a creature is present. You open your senses to numerous visions of the immediate future. The visions grant you subtle details of your immediate surroundings within 30 feet. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Three Pecks of Dew](/Feats.aspx?ID=7092) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 115

**Archetype** [Cultivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=278)

**Prerequisites**
[Cultivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7085); you aren't [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)

</column>

---

At this stage of cultivation, your body is as much spirit as flesh. While still fettered to the physical realm, your form flourishes without needing conventional food or drink, and your natural healing now rivals that brought by scalpel and suture.

You become [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait. When you perform the [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) downtime activity, you can use [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) for the skill check (instead of the skills normally associated with your environment). If you do so, this activity gains the [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) trait as you subsist on ambient qi within your environment’s dew-laden air and create shelter from solidified emanations of qi.

Additionally, when you [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621), you can also [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) at the same time. If you do so, you can use Occultism for checks to Treat Wounds and disregard the need for a [healer’s kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727); this activity gains the vitality trait as you circulate healing qi through your own body or transfuse your ally with healing qi.

<title level="2">Three Pecks of Dew leads to...</title>
[The Immortal Attains the Summit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7094)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 51

</column>

---

You’ve trained to use unique nagaji eating habits to your advantage. By manipulating your throat muscles, you can create a pocket of air to store up to four items of light Bulk or less without risk of dissolving. None of these items can have a dimension longer than 1 foot. As long as you have at least one item in your throat pocket, your speech is noticeably difficult to understand, and you have a visible bulge in your neck. Placing an item in your throat pocket or retrieving one is an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action. You can empty your throat pocket with a single action, causing everything you had stored in it to fall to the ground in your square. Any item that was covered in dirt or grime comes out clean.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Throw and Catch](/Feats.aspx?ID=8188) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 87

**Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341)

**Prerequisites**
[Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178)

**Requirements**
You are wielding a melee warshard weapon.

</column>

---

You hurl your warshard weapon at an opponent, even though the weapon isn’t designed to be thrown. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). Your weapon gains the [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) trait with a range increment of 40 feet; if your weapon already has the thrown trait, increase its range increment by 40 feet. Make a ranged Strike at mythic proficiency at an opponent within range. For this ranged Strike, apply your full Strength modifier to the damage, as if it were a melee Strike. After the Strike resolves, the weapon flies back to your hand, and you can then attempt a melee Strike (at your normal proficiency, not mythic proficiency) against a target in reach of your weapon. Both attacks count toward your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289), but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both attacks.

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Thunder Clap](/Feats.aspx?ID=3576) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=147" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Martial Artist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=67)

**Prerequisites**
[Powder Punch Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3575)

**Requirements**
You're in Powder Punch Stance.

</column>

---

You slam your hands together to unleash a deafening blast. Creatures in a 15-foot cone take 3d6 sonic damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC. Creatures that critically fail their save are also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 minute. You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds as your hands recover from the thunderous vibrations.

 At 8th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage from Thunder Clap increases by 1d6.

<title level="2">Black Powder Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 55

If the characters agree to Nixbrix's challenge to defeat Bitey or otherwise impress the gang leader, he offers to teach them a few tricks. The characters gain access to the feats in the Black-Powder Berserkers section on page 79, even if they aren't from Alkenstar or the Mana Wastes, though they still must meet the feats' other prerequisites to take them.

**Related Feats**: [Black Powder Flash](/Feats.aspx?ID=3572), [Inured to Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=3573), [Pain Tolerance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3574), [Powder Punch Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3575)

    right="Feat 14"

>
[Thwart Evil](/Feats.aspx?ID=3610) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Lastwall Sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882); Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

**Trigger**
A creature you can see uses a spell or ability that has the [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64) or [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) traits.

</column>

---

You react instinctively when you sense evil forming, thrusting your spiritual energy toward the source to snuff out evil before it fully manifests. Attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell or ability using your Religion modifier as your counteract modifier.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tidal Hands](/Feats.aspx?ID=4268) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 32

</column>

---

With an emphatic gesture, you create waves that rush out from you in the shape of your hands. You either form two 15-foot cones that don't overlap or you combine the hands into one 30-foot cone. Each creature in a wave takes 1d8 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. If a creature critically fails, you also [push](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) that creature 5 feet.

---
**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d8.

    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tidal Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=2616) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Undine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=314" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 119

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You conjure the force of the tides to gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC until the end of your next turn. Any allies adjacent to you during the duration gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC as long as they remain adjacent to you. You can Sustain the effect to a maximum duration of 5 rounds. When a creature receiving a circumstance bonus to AC from Tidal Shield would take damage from an attack, as a reaction, you can reduce the damage to that creature by 40; after you do so, Tidal Shield ends.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"

[Tidal Wave](/Feats.aspx?ID=8928) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 97

**Archetype** [Undersea Privateer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=379)

**Prerequisites**
[Undersea Privateer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8915)

</column>

---

Like the ocean in a storm, you overwhelm your opponents with speed and force. Move up to your Speed and make two Strikes. These Strikes can happen at any point during your movement. If either Strike reduces a target to 0 Hit Points, you gain the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) condition for 1 round. You can only use the extra action to Stride or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381).

You enter the stance of a tiger and can make tiger claw attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, finesse, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. On a critical success with your tiger claws, if you deal damage, the target takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage.

 As long as your Speed is at least 20 feet while in Tiger Stance, you can Step 10 feet.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Time Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3839) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 184

**Archetype** [Time Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=191)

**Prerequisites**
You have a spellcasting class feature.

</column>

---

You might be a novice in the temporal arts now, but in the future, you'll hold time in the palm of your hand. As some of your future knowledge leaks back to your present self, you gain the [_delay consequence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=622) domain spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. This feat grants a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover by using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to revisit moments from your past and contemplate futures yet to come. If you already knew _delay consequence_ from a feat or ability that allows you to gain your choice of domain spell, such as [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=265), then when you take this feat, you can retrain that option to gain a different domain spell instead as your personal timeline rearranges itself. You also gain [_time sense_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1193) as an innate cantrip usable at will. This innate spell and your focus spells from the time mage archetype are of the same tradition as the spells you used to meet the archetype's prerequisites.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the time mage archetype.

<title level="2">Time Mage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Chronocognizance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3840), [Chronomancer's Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3841), [Future Spell Learning](/Feats.aspx?ID=3842), [Into the Future](/Feats.aspx?ID=3844), [Purge of Moments](/Feats.aspx?ID=3845), [Timeline-Splitting Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3846), [What Could Have Been](/Feats.aspx?ID=3843)

[Timelessness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8177) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 83

**Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340)

**Prerequisites**
[Timewracked Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8166)

</column>

---

Time travelers are rare, but even among them your isolation from time is unique. As long as you remain timewracked, you do not age and cannot die of natural causes. You’re immune to hostile spells and effects related to time or aging, as well as the [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) condition (except for when you gain the slowed condition through this mythic destiny). You reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1. Whenever you roll a flat check to end persistent damage, you roll twice and choose your desired result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect. In addition, your intimate knowledge of the flow of time gives you a measure of influence over the attempt of another to manipulate it. Whenever an enemy creature that you are aware of and who is within 60 feet of you gains the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) condition, you gain the quickened condition for 1 round. The actions available to you from the acquired condition are the same as those granted by the ability that quickens your enemy.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 185

**Archetype** [Time Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=191)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Time Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3839)

</column>

---

You invest in two futures, then choose the one to make a reality. You Cast two Spells that each take 1 or 2 actions to cast. These can't be the same spell heightened to two different levels. You expend the resources for both spells, such as spell slots, Focus Points, and material components. Determine the immediate results for both spells, including attack rolls, saving throws, damage, and any other dice rolls. Then, choose which of the two spells takes effect, using the previously made rolls. The other spell's resources are still expended, but the spell has no effect as the magic disappears the other timeline.

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340)

</column>

---

The current of time shifts subtly in your field of view. You have learned to tread these temporal eddies, moving forward and pushing backward in small strokes—sometimes even gaining the ability to move your allies and enemies through time as you choose. Whether or not you’ll ever be fully restored to your proper timeline, you can’t predict—but until then you continue to manipulate your estrangement from time to move unseen, defy your opponents in combat, and occupy future or past versions of yourself to escape distress. With practice you could gain the ability to rehearse a speech at the same tie you deliver it or attack distant foes without spending the time to move between them. Eventually, you might gain the power to vanish from existence altogether while you hop forward and backward in time or even become immortal.

Your Speed increases by 5 feet for each mode of movement available to you. You can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) to roll any check made to determine your initiative at mythic proficiency. If your initiative roll result is tied with an opponent’s initiative roll, you can choose to go first. In addition, you gain the following reaction. 

<document level="2" id="action-3531" />

[Be Right Back](/Feats.aspx?ID=8167), [Bolstered Recovery](/Feats.aspx?ID=8172), [Fracture Time Flow](/Feats.aspx?ID=8175), [Live Off Borrowed Time](/Feats.aspx?ID=8168), [Not This Time](/Feats.aspx?ID=8176), [Now You See Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=8169), [Preserve the Moment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8174), [Second Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=8170), [Temporal Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=8171), [Timelessness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8177)

>
[Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 79

**Archetypes** [Druid](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=6), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) (Level 20), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=218) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Your mask hosts the legacy of Golden Snake, the Tireless Guide, allowing you to guide others with ease. Your allies can use [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) to follow you for any of your trained skills, in addition to skills in which you are an expert or better. When they follow you when you use a trained skill, their circumstance bonus is +1. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one ally, that ally can Stride as a free action.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

>
[To Me!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8164) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

Two lives spent in adventuring groups has given you a special gift for bolstering party morale and pushing your allies to achieve greater ends when they work as a team. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) to rally your allies to your side to regroup or push your advantage. Stride and then make a melee Strike. As soon as your turn is over, your allies within 30 feet who can see and hear you may Stride in your direction as a free action, but don’t have to. Your allies control their own movement and may move in such a way as to avoid obstacles or creatures, but if they Stride, they must be at least 5 feet closer to you than where they were when they started by the end of this movement. If yours or an ally’s movement this round triggers reactions, you or your ally uses mythic proficiency to determine their AC or to attempt a saving throw to resist the reaction. If an ally is within melee range of the target of the Strike you made with this ability, that ally may also make a melee Strike against that enemy as a reaction instead of Striding toward you.

Any Strikes from To Me! made against your nemesis, be they Strikes you make or Strikes made by allies, use mythic proficiency.

Your ability to track your prey has surpassed explanation, allowing you to trace your prey’s movements and predict its location with ease. When you use Hunt Prey on a creature within 100 feet, you can follow that creature’s movements, allowing you to know the creature’s exact location no matter how far away it becomes, as long as it remains your prey. You must be legendary in Nature to track your prey’s location across teleportation or planar travel. This feat gains the detection and primal traits if you’re legendary in Nature.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[To War!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7312) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 108

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304)

**Requirements**
You are riding your apocalypse [mount](/Actions.aspx?ID=2314).

</column>

---

You inspire your allies to greater battle prowess while trampling enemies in your way. You Command your apocalypse mount to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to twice its Speed (or to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), if it has the corresponding movement type), moving through the space of any foes in your path up to one size smaller than your apocalypse mount. Your mount deals damage equal to one of its unarmed attack [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) to each creature whose space you move through (basic Reflex save against your apocalypse mount’s [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) DC). On a critical failure, the creature also becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your next turn. You can damage a given creature only once during this movement.

In addition, all allies who witnessed your charge gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level and a +2 status bonus to damage against any foe damaged by your apocalypse mount this round.     right="Feat 12"

>
[Too Angry to Die](/Feats.aspx?ID=3899) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 9

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

**Trigger**
you stand up from [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) after waking up from being [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You refuse to yield the battle, even after you've been knocked off your feet and nearly killed. For you, such a brush with death is less something to fear and more a thing to become infuriated by. As you stand up, you roar in defiance and can attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) a foe.

<title level="2">Adventuring with Amiri</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 8

As Amiri explores the Stolen Lands, her legend grows with her. Already a larger-than-life personality, she begins to accidentally encourage something akin to a cult of personality in the PCs' kingdom. If brought to her attention that a new generation of adventurers are using her exploits and legends as an inspiration for their own adventuring style, she's amused but also perhaps a bit put off by the idea.

 The following new skill feats become available to the PCs starting at 4th level, assuming Amiri remains allied with them.

**Related Feats**: [Say that Again!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3898), [That's Not Natural!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3897), [Triumphant Boast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3896)

While you might be small enough to grab normally, you can change that at a moment's notice. You cast [_untamed form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1861). ---

When you observe an ally try and fail to execute a strategic maneuver against your enemies, you coordinate with your other allies to finish the job, using the opening from the first attempt to keep your foe off-balance and ensure your eventual success.

 When an ally within your overwatch field attempts to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) an opponent within your overwatch field and fails, you coordinate efforts to provide a +2 circumstance bonus to the next [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check rolled by a different ally to attempt the same action on the same target before that target's next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Topple the Titans](/Feats.aspx?ID=8009) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #217: Death Sails a Wine-Dark Sea
](/Sources.aspx?ID=273) pg. 79

**Frequency**
Once per minute

**Requirements**
Your previous action was a successful or critically successful [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) against a creature at least one size larger than you, and the enemy became [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

</column>

---

Even the greatest titans of the world are easier to kill when they’re lying on the ground. You’ve made it your mission to topple such giants and can make others fall with a force that shakes the very earth. The triggering creature’s toppling body shakes the ground, emitting a quake in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) from their space. Apply the result of your triggering [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check against the Reflex DC of each creature in the emanation to Trip them as well. You do not need to have a hand free, and you do not lose your balance if any of your attempts to Trip are a critical failure.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Toppling Tentacles](/Feats.aspx?ID=3391) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_black tentacles_](/Spells.aspx?ID=23)

</column>

---

When you cast _black tentacles_, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: Tentacles slither along the ground in the area, attempting to hinder anyone within. Sticky black tentacles attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) each creature in the area. Attempt spell attack rolls against the Reflex DCs of each affected creature. Any creature you succeed against is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage. Whenever a creature ends its turn in the area, the tentacles attempt to Trip that creature if it isn't already prone, and they deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage to any creature already prone. Creatures treat the spell's area as difficult terrain.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Torch Goblin](/Feats.aspx?ID=1005) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 38

**Prerequisites**
[Charhide Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=16) heritage

</column>

---

You’ve spent enough time on fire that you know how to use it to your advantage. You can light yourself thoroughly on fire with a held [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60), a bottle of [alchemist’s fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75), or a similar incendiary, dealing yourself 1d6 persistent fire damage. As long as you are suffering persistent fire damage, all your melee attacks against adjacent creatures deal an additional 1 fire damage per weapon damage die. Any creature that successfully [Grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), [Shoves](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), or [Trips](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) you takes 1d6 fire damage; if it uses a weapon for that action, the weapon takes the damage instead. You must still attempt the flat check to remove the persistent fire damage each round, as normal.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**There is a more recent version of this, [click here to view.](/Feats.aspx?ID=4079)**

**Source** [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 77, [Fists of the Ruby Phoenix Hardcover](/Sources.aspx?ID=193) pg. 223

**Archetype** [Sixth Pillar](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=94)

**Prerequisites**
[Sixth Pillar Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2739)

</column>

---

You can redirect a spell's power through you to deliver it within striking distance. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with 1 or more targets and a range farther than touch, you can change the range to touch. If the altered spell requires a spell attack roll, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack. This only allows you to touch a single target with the spell, even if the spell originally affected more than 1 target. After you Cast the Spell, you can [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40), or Strike the target with an unarmed attack.

In moments of viciousness, your curse can partially infect your prey. </title>

<traits>

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Your skin is medium armor in the [plate](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=4) armor group that grants a +4 item bonus to AC, and has a Dex cap of +1, a check penalty of –2, a Speed penalty of –5 feet, a Strength value of 16, and the [comfort](/Traits.aspx?ID=203) trait. You can never wear other armor or remove your hide. You can etch armor runes onto your hide.

 If you're a lethoci kashrishi who takes this feat, your modifications also make you more buoyant, allowing you to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) across the surface of even turbulent bodies of water without needing to make an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check.

**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into this feat.

You’ve taken your share of licks while scurrying around the battlefield and know how to defend yourself against opportunistic attackers. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=286)

</column>

---

When you cast _sigil_, you can modify the spell to add the following to its standard effects: The target leaves a magical trail that you and others can try to follow. You and other creatures can attempt to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the target, substituting an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check (whichever matches the magical tradition of your sigil spell) for the [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check. Much like Tracking with Survival, this must take place somewhere the target has been and follow the trail; it doesn't allow anyone to find the target from a distance. You can only have a single target marked with a modified sigil in this way. If you use this ability again on a second target, the _sigil_ spell on the first target ends, and your mark fades.

<title level="2">Tracing Sigil leads to...</title>
[Beacon Mark](/Feats.aspx?ID=3383)

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 264 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) --- You spend time teaching an animal to do a certain action. You can either select a basic action the animal already knows how to do (typically those listed in the Command an Animal action on page 242) or attempt to teach the animal a new basic action. The GM determines the DC of any check required and the amount of time the training takes (usually at least a week). It’s usually impossible to teach an animal a trick that uses critical thinking. If you’re expert, master, or legendary in Nature, you might be able to train more unusual creatures, at the GM’s discretion. **Success** The animal learns the action. If it was an action the animal already knew, you can Command the Animal to take that action without attempting a Nature check. If it was a new basic action, add that action to the actions the animal can take when Commanded, but you must still roll.
**Failure** The animal doesn’t learn the trick.

    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Trample](/Feats.aspx?ID=6929) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sarangay" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=829" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 63

</column>

---

You know how to leverage your size and momentum when using your horns attack, and can use your movement speed to overrun your foes. You [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to double your Speed and can move through the spaces of creatures at least one size smaller than you, Trampling each creature whose space you enter. You can attempt to Trample the same creature only once in a single Trample. You deal piercing damage equal to the damage of your horns unarmed attack against these creatures, which can attempt a basic Reflex save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

>
[Trampling Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1927) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 165

**Archetypes** [Cavalier](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=53), [Mammoth Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=170) (Level 12)

**Prerequisites**
[Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1919)

**Requirements**
You are riding a mount that has a melee Strike using its legs (claw, talons, hoof, etc.).

</column>

---

You urge your mount forward, trampling enemies in your path. You command your mount to Stride up to its Speed (or to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39), if it has the corresponding movement type), moving through the spaces of any foes in your path up to one size smaller than your mount. Your mount deals damage equal to the melee Strike using its legs to each creature whose space you move through, subject to a basic Reflex save against your mount's [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) DC. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the end of your next turn. You can damage a given creature only once during this movement.

Finally, if you become cursebound 4 at any point during this duration, this bonus increases to a +20-foot status bonus.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 29

</column>

---

Your protean vitality is fecund and many-succoring: your veins run with life-giving ichor that adapts to the blood and physiology of any body, and your skin molts on command, creating wound-stanching sheaths of tissue for yourself and others. You become trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9). If you were already trained in Medicine, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54) without [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) by using your physiology instead, but you must take 1 damage to make the attempt. Similarly, you can [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57) without healer's tools but take 2d8 damage. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus on all Medicine checks to Administer First Aid and Treat Wounds using your own physiology.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 169, [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 107

**Archetypes** [Archaeologist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=46) (Level 4), [Archaeologist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=237) (Level 4)

</column>

---

You have an intuitive sense that alerts you to the presence of traps. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps, to AC against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps. Even if you aren’t Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

You can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of master in Thievery. If you have master proficiency in Thievery, you can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of legendary instead, and your circumstance bonuses against traps increase to +2.

---

You use glimmering gears and gnashing mechanisms to manufacture [snares](/Equipment.aspx?Category=31) using specialized parts. Your snares include clockwork and steam-powered cogwheels and gears, and their gush of steam can hinder those you ensnare. If you choose to construct a snare using gears and a creature fails their saving throw against the snare, all creatures are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to that creature for 1 round, as a burst of steam obscures its vision.

<title level="2">Trapsmith Dedication leads to...</title>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 81

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You can undo the effect of demonic corruption in plants. By spending 10 minutes in contact with a tree that’s been corrupted by demonic presence, you can restore the tree to its original health. This does not prevent that tree from becoming corrupted again in the future. Alternatively, you can spend 10 minutes in contact with a creature with the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) trait. At the end of this time, you restore 7d8+56 Hit Points to that creature and heal half that amount of your own Hit Points. Additionally, you can attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) any one [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) afflicting that plant creature as if you had cast [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) heightened to 7th rank. Your counteract rank for this is 7, and your counteract check is equal to your Will save or your spell attack modifier, whichever is higher.

---

Your lips murmur as you portend a great disaster, one you hope you survive. A rain of blazing bolts begins to fall from the heavens in a 10-foot emanation, centered on you, that deals 2d6 fire damage to all creatures in the emanation at the end of each of your turns (basic Reflex save); you can't exclude yourself from the emanation. The skyfire persists for 1 minute; while you can't [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it, you can suppress the effect for 1 round with a [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) action. The rain of fire is suppressed if you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95). If you become [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) 3 or 4 at any point during Trial by Skyfire's duration, the emanation increases to 15 feet and the damage increases to 4d6.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 131

**Prerequisites**
[Monastic Archer Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1734); [Stunning Fist](/Feats.aspx?ID=442)

**Requirements**
You are in Monastic Archer Stance and wielding a bow usable with that stance.

</column>

---

You string three arrows to your bow and fire them all at once. Make three ranged Strikes against a single target with the required weapon, each using your current multiple attack penalty, and you take an additional –2 penalty. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty, and you combine the attacks' damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Your Stunning Fist benefit applies to Triangle Shot, even though it isn't a [Flurry of Blows](/Actions.aspx?ID=9). If all three Strikes hit, the target takes 3d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

Your spotter's quick signals help you make even difficult shots seem simple. You are equally at home piloting any [vehicle](/Vehicles.aspx), adapting yourself instantly to varied controls, movements, and handling. Whenever piloting a vehicle requires a [Piloting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Sailing Lore check, you can use your Driving Lore proficiency instead. You can use Dexterity in place of Intelligence when attempting piloting checks with Driving Lore. You become an expert in Driving Lore. At 7th level, you become a master in Driving Lore, and at 15th level, you become legendary in Driving Lore.

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 264 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) --- You examine a magic item you normally couldn’t use in an effort to fool it and activate it temporarily. For example, this might allow a fighter to cast a spell from a wand or allow a wizard to cast a spell that’s not on the arcane list using a scroll. You must know what activating the item does, or you can’t attempt to trick it. Attempt a check using the skill matching the item’s magic tradition, or matching a tradition that has the spell on its list, if you’re trying to cast a spell from the item. The relevant skills are Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, Religion for divine, or any of the four for an item that has the magical trait and not a tradition trait. The GM determines the DC based on the item’s level (possibly adjusted depending on the item or situation). If you activate a magic item that requires a spell attack modifier or spell DC and you don’t have proficiency in the relevant statistic, use your level as your proficiency bonus and the highest of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifiers. If you’re a master in the appropriate skill for the item’s tradition, you instead use the trained proficiency bonus; if you’re legendary, you instead use the expert proficiency bonus. **Success** For the rest of the current turn, you can spend actions to activate the item as if you could normally use it.
**Failure** You can’t use the item or try to trick it again this turn, but you can try again on subsequent turns.
**Critical Failure** You can’t use the item, and you can’t try to trick it again until your next daily preparations.

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 116 **Archetypes** [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=117) (Level 12), [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120) (Level 12), [Unexpected Sharpshooter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=123) (Level 10), [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=364) (Level 12), [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=367) (Level 12), [Unexpected Sharpshooter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=370) (Level 10) **Requirements** You're wielding a loaded crossbow or firearm. --- You shoot not at your foe but at an object nearby. Make a Strike with your firearm against an AC equal to an easy DC for your level. On a success, instead of hitting your foe, your attack hits an object behind or to the side of your target, creating one of the following effects. The GM might determine that a different AC is appropriate or that a particular effect isn't a valid option, such as using the explosive barrel option when there's no such object on the battlefield. The GM should inform you if a Trick Shot is feasible before you spend your actions, since your trained eye can easily recognize loose or volatile objects.
  • **Dislodge Object** Your attack knocks an unattended object of no more than 2 Bulk out of position, moving it up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. For example, the weapon could knock a wizard's crystal ball off a table.
  • **Explosive Barrel** Your attack strikes a barrel of expensive rum, a vial of volatile alchemical fluids, a demonic pustule erupting from the earth, or some other explosive object. The object explodes in a 20-foot burst, and creatures in the area take 6d6 damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. The damage type is chosen by the GM, based on the exploding object. Increase the damage by 1d6 for every 2 levels you have above 10th.
Trick Shot leads to... [Ranged Disarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3239)

>
[Trickster's Ace](/Feats.aspx?ID=5973) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 113

**Trigger**
You specify the trigger when you make your daily preparations.

**Requirements**
When you make your daily preparations, you must specify a trigger for this reaction using the same restrictions as the triggers for the [Ready](/Actions.aspx?ID=2299) action. You also choose a single spell from the arcane, divine, occult, or primal list of 4th level or lower. The spell can’t have a cost, nor can its casting time be more than 10 minutes. The spell must be able to target a single creature, and you must be a valid target for it.

</column>

---

Whether from jury-rigged magic items, deduction from the study of magical interactions, or other means, you have a contingency in your back pocket for desperate situations. When the trigger occurs, you cause the spell to come into effect. The spell targets only you, no matter how many creatures it would affect normally. If you define particularly complicated conditions, as determined by the GM, the trigger might fail. Once the contingency is triggered, the spell is expended until your next daily preparations.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 92

**Archetype** [Spirit Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=274)

**Prerequisites**
[Spirit Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7020)

</column>

---

You’ve sworn an oath to ferret out and destroy malevolent shapechangers who pose as mortals with evil intent. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to detect a shapechanged creature’s disguise, and a +2 circumstance bonus to attempts to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about shapechangers. Whenever you use Overwhelming Combination against a shapechanged creature, you attempt to counteract one polymorph effect on that creature. The counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check modifier is your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus with the weapon used to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) as part of your Overwhelming Combination. You gain the following edict.

**Edict** You must reveal and slay evil or predatory shapechangers you discover or encounter, as long as you have a reasonable chance of success.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 108

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[way of the triggerbrand](/Ways.aspx?ID=6)

**Requirements**
You're wielding a [combination](/Traits.aspx?ID=417) weapon.

</column>

---

You dance through your foes, stabbing and shooting. You Stride, making up to three Strikes with your combination weapon at any point during your movement, each against a different target. You can make any combination of melee and ranged attacks without needing to change modes to do so, though typically you can't make more than one ranged attack because of the need to reload. This counts as three attacks toward your multiple attack penalty, but you don't apply the multiple attack penalty until after making all three attacks. 

After using Triggerbrand Blitz, you become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) for 1 minute.

You can use your webbed feet to guide your fall. You glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down (10 feet if you don't have both hands free) and up to 25 feet forward through the air.
