fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Triumphant Boast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3896) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 9

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

You relate a loud and impressive tale of your triumph over a formidable foe. When you [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59), choose a single target within 30 feet of you and compare the result of your Performance check to that observer's Will DC. If you're a master in Performance, you can choose up to four targets, and if you're legendary, you can choose any number of targets. If you succeed, any attempt made by you to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) that creature within the next 24 hours gains a +1 circumstance bonus. If your Charisma score is 20 or higher and you're a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2. Once a creature is boasted at in this manner, it becomes temporarily immune to further Triumphant Boasts for 24 hours.

<title level="2">Adventuring with Amiri</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 8

As Amiri explores the Stolen Lands, her legend grows with her. Already a larger-than-life personality, she begins to accidentally encourage something akin to a cult of personality in the PCs' kingdom. If brought to her attention that a new generation of adventurers are using her exploits and legends as an inspiration for their own adventuring style, she's amused but also perhaps a bit put off by the idea.

 The following new skill feats become available to the PCs starting at 4th level, assuming Amiri remains allied with them.

**Related Feats**: [Say that Again!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3898), [That's Not Natural!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3897), [Too Angry to Die](/Feats.aspx?ID=3899)

    right="Feat 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tumbling Diversion](/Feats.aspx?ID=5629) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kobold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=759" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 23

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Attempt to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an opponent's space. If you succeed or critically succeed and don't end your movement adjacent to that opponent, you can attempt to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387) to distract that opponent. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Deception check (or a +2 circumstance bonus if you critically succeeded at the Acrobatics check to Tumble Through) to Create a Diversion. If you succeed or critically succeed to Create a Diversion, you become [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) to only the creature whose space you Tumbled Through.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 34 --- A slew of logs eject from the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) and slam into your enemies. They roll in a 10-foot-wide, 30-foot-long line. Non-magical [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) on any ground the logs roll over is smashed flat; greater difficult terrain remains. Each creature in the area takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and might be moved by the logs, depending on its Reflex save against your class DC. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) out of the line in the most direct path available.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). --- **Level (+3)** The damage increases by 1d8.

<traits>

<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 155

**Archetype** [Acrobat](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=45)

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Acrobat Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1873)

**Requirements**

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 155 **Archetype** [Acrobat](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=45) **Prerequisites** [Acrobat Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1873) **Requirements** You are adjacent to an enemy. --- Attempt an Acrobatics check against the Reflex DC of an enemy adjacent to you. **Critical Success** You move through the enemy's space to an unoccupied space on the other side of the enemy from your starting position. This movement doesn't trigger reactions. You can't move farther than your Speed, and you must end your movement adjacent to the enemy whose space you moved through. After moving, you make a melee Strike against the enemy whose space you moved through, and the enemy is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against that Strike.
**Success** As critical success, but the enemy isn't flat-footed against the Strike.
**Failure** You remain in your original space but can still Strike.
**Critical Failure** No effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 77

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); Expert in [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17)

</column>

---

You reach for an opponent's item as you move past a foe. If you critically succeed your check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) an enemy's space, you can attempt to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) something from the enemy as a reaction. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Thievery check to Steal as your tumbling makes it difficult for your enemy to keep track of your movement. You can Steal any immediately accessible item of light or lighter Bulk on the enemy's person, such as a potion or coin purse hanging from a belt, but not anything inside a container or anything the enemy is holding. The GM has final say on what you can Steal.

[Tunnel Roll](/Feats.aspx?ID=5391) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=658" />
<trait label="Surki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=789" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 50

</column>

---

You can more easily navigate underground tunnels by rolling up into a ball. You roll up and move up to four times your Speed in a straight line down an incline. If you reach the bottom of the incline or hit an obstacle during this first turn of movement, you stop rolling. Otherwise, you automatically keep rolling at this Speed during subsequent turns until you hit the bottom of the incline or an obstacle ends this movement (which can happen in the middle of your turn). You're [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) each turn after the first that you keep rolling; if you hit an obstacle on a turn after the first, you and the obstacle both take 4d6 bludgeoning damage, and you stop rolling.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 80

**Prerequisites**
[Ghoul Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504); Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

You have elongated claws and enhanced senses, making you uncanny at digging the underground passageways needed to construct ghoul warrens and rob graves without arousing suspicion. You gain a burrow Speed of 15 feet and a [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) of 60 feet. You can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) through any earthen matter, including rock, while moving at your full burrow Speed. When you move in this way, you can choose either to leave tunnels behind you that are large enough to allow creatures of your size or smaller to move through them or move through the ground while leaving no tunnels or signs of your passing.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 13

**Prerequisites**
You have a spellcasting class feature with the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) or [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) tradition

**Access**
Erutaki ethnicity

</column>

---

You know the truth behind old stories that tell of sending a fetish of bone and sinew to seek vengeance. These old magics allow you to conjure constructs with ease. Add the [_summon construct_](/Spells.aspx?ID=318) spell to your spell list. The constructs you summon have a distinct ivory scrimshaw appearance, and if you include a drop of blood, lock of hair, or other portion of a creature’s body as part of the spell’s material component, the summoned construct gains a +4 status bonus to Perception checks to sense or locate that creature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 43

**Trigger**
You would attempt a roll affected by a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect.

</column>

---

You perform a superstition, such as casting salt over your shoulder to ward off bad luck. Turn Away Misfortune's [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) trait cancels out the misfortune effect, causing you to roll normally. As normal, you can apply only one fortune ability to a roll, so if you Turned Away Misfortune on an attack roll, you couldn't also use an ability like [Halfling Luck](/Feats.aspx?ID=54) to alter the roll further.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Turn the Wheel of Seasons](/Feats.aspx?ID=4295) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 35

</column>

---

The seasons shift rapidly. This impulse affects a cube 100 feet in each dimension within 1,000 feet. Choose the starting season. The impulse lasts for 4 rounds, proceeding to the next season at the start of each of your turns. You can't use this impulse again until the previous one ends.

 **Spring** Each ally in the cube gains 20 temporary HP that last until the start of your next turn. Any [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) ally rolls a [recovery check](/Rules.aspx?ID=375), but can't get worse than a success.

 **Summer** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100)) Each enemy in the area is exposed to sunlight and must attempt a Reflex save against your class DC. It's unaffected on a critical success, [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the start of your next turn on a success, or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) until the start of your next turn on a failure.

 **Autumn** Leaves and rain make everything in the area [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) until the start of your next turn, and a cold wind makes each enemy in the area [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until the start of your next turn unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save against your class DC.

 **Winter** Each enemy in the aura takes 5d6 cold damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that fails its save also takes 2d6 [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

---

Your logging training has made you intimately familiar with all aspects of forestry, and you have trained extensively to reach around trees and utilize their bulk to your advantage. You become trained in [Milling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and Forest Lore, or an expert if you were already trained. You can always [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=90) when you are within forest terrain to gain cover, even if you’re not next to an obstacle you can Take Cover behind. In addition, any enemy who gains standard cover from a tree gains only lesser cover against your attacks (or only standard cover, if the enemy otherwise gains greater cover).

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Turpin Rowe lumberjack archetype.

You have particularly long, jagged tusks perfect for tearing meat from bone. You gain a tusks unarmed attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. Your tusks are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits.

The Sapphire Butterfly is not one for violence when simply intimidating a foe will do. From that vigilante's techniques, you've learned how to pull a deadly blow at the last moment, threatening your target instead of striking them. Rather than dealing damage with the triggering Strike, attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check with a +2 circumstance bonus to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) all enemies within 30 feet who can see you. If you critically succeed at your check to Demoralize the target of your Strike, their attitude toward you improves by one step while they also become [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).

---

You spend 1 minute making quick adjustments to someone’s clothing and appearance, causing their words to carry more weight with an audience of your choice. While speaking to that audience, the target gains a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. If you have master proficiency in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), the bonus increases to +2; if you have legendary proficiency in Crafting, the bonus increases to +3. This bonus lasts until this ability is used on the target again, the situation they were prepared for ends, or they next change their outfit.

<title level="2">Lacunafex Lore</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 72

If the PCs earn Mialari Docur's trust and prove their worth by defeating the Scarlet Triad, she rewards them by granting them access to several feats and spells she and her students have developed over the years.

**Access**

</column>

---

Few would even suspect that you're a member of the Eagle Knights, and you use the tricks of the spymaster's trade to keep it that way. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Espionage Lore. If you were already trained in Espionage Lore, you also become trained in a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill of your choice. 

During your daily preparations, you can brush up on a specific field to gain the trained proficiency rank in one Lore skill of your choice. This proficiency lasts until you prepare again. Since this proficiency is temporary, you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat. If you have master proficiency in Espionage Lore, you gain expert proficiency in the chosen skill instead, and if you have legendary proficiency in Espionage Lore, you gain master proficiency in the skill.

**Special** You can take this dedication even if you haven't taken more than two non-dedication feats from the [Eagle Knight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314) archetype.

<title level="2">Twilight Talon Dedication leads to...</title>
[Burn Identity](/Feats.aspx?ID=8867), [Deceptive Deduction](/Feats.aspx?ID=8862), [Fabricated Credentials](/Feats.aspx?ID=8861), [Feign Innocence](/Feats.aspx?ID=8865), [Hidden Intentions](/Feats.aspx?ID=8863), [Make Do](/Feats.aspx?ID=8860), [Talon's Mark](/Feats.aspx?ID=8859)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twin Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=2944) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=392" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 73

</column>

---

You can transform to match your eidolon. When you [Manifest your Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757), you can call upon its powers to transform yourself into a duplicate until it unmanifests. You can't use this if you Manifest your Eidolon in an unusual way, such as [Meld into Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=2892). While using Twin Eidolon, you use your eidolon's statistics other than your mental ability modifiers, including its evolutions. You can't cast spells (except spells your eidolon could cast), Activate or otherwise benefit from magic items that normally benefit you and not your eidolon, or use other actions it can't perform. Any of its spells you cast with limited uses count against your eidolon's uses. You can Manifest your Eidolon again to end this effect.

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your eidolon's tradition ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twin Stars](/Feats.aspx?ID=7156) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 35

**Usage**
imbued into a one-handed weapon ikon

</column>

---

Your divine spark embodies a primordial duality, and your ikon splits itself accordingly into two corresponding halves. You can use an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to split the imbued ikon into two copies of itself, which both gain the [twin](/Traits.aspx?ID=717) trait; these copies are identical except for one mirrored feature, such as a sun motif on one and a moon motif on another. You can use this ability again to fuse the two halves back into their original form. As these are both manifestations of the same object, your divine spark empowers the two halves as if they were a single ikon.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twin Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3719) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
mortal weakness or personal antithesis

**Requirements**
You're holding an [implement](/Implements.aspx) and a weapon, you are using [Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227) with mortal weakness or personal antithesis, and the target creature is within reach of both your implement and weapon.

</column>

---

As you make an attack augmented by your esoterica, you also press your implement against the creature, applying its weakness as your implement's energies sear the creature's flesh. Make a melee Strike against the target of your Exploit Vulnerability. On any attack roll result but a critical failure, you also press your implement against the creature, automatically dealing the additional damage from Exploit Vulnerability. This is in addition to any damage from your Strike, including the weakness the Strike applies from Exploit Vulnerability. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twisting Petal Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7107) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Martial Artist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=255) (Level 4)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

**Requirements**
You're [unarmored](/Armor.aspx?ID=38).

</column>

---

Your body moves like a petal twisting on the wind, confounding your opponents while using their energy against them. You can make gale blossom strikes that deal 1d6 slashing damage. These strikes are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661), [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=694), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) traits. While in Twisting Petal Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) and a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC to avoid being Shoved. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) and a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception DC to resist an opponent’s Feint attempt.

<title level="2">Twisting Petal Stance leads to...</title>
[Scattering in Spring](/Feats.aspx?ID=7111), [Whirling in the Summer Storm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7113)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Two-Element Infusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=4193) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Infusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=503" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 22

**Prerequisites**
two or more kinetic elements

</column>

---

Slamming one element into another, you combine their strengths. If the next action you use is an [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125), choose two of your kinetic elements instead of one. The blast gains the traits of both elements and uses the highest range and damage die among the two elements. Half the blast's damage is the damage type of one element, and the other half is the damage type of the other element. If the total damage is an odd number, you choose which element deals the higher damage. Determine the damage amounts before altering the amount due to halving, doubling, resistances, weaknesses, and other calculations. If either element can deal more than one type of damage, you can still choose which damage type to use. You gain any added effects of both elements, such as their critical blast junction effects.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Two-Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=3802) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Reflection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=431" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 121

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Your ability to imitate your progenitor is so strong, you can even convince yourself. You prepare a variety of incredible gizmos on each of your allies, linking them together through careful modification to enable you to power them up all at once. During your daily preparations, select up to six willing allies. Whenever you Overdrive, you grant the benefits of your overdrive to any of these allies you choose who are within 30 feet of you. The allies don't gain the increased damage from expert, master, or legendary overdrive.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Share Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3717)

</column>

---

You've nurtured your bonds with your comrades, allowing you to share the benefits of your esoterica. When you use [Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227) and choose mortal weakness, select any number of allies within 30 feet of you. Their Strikes apply the weakness from mortal weakness the same way your Strikes do. This benefit ends when you stop benefiting from Exploit Vulnerability. Since this effect depends on magically strengthening your bond to your allies, only allies with whom you've developed a rapport over the course of one or more days gain the benefit.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 172

**Archetype** [Ulfen Guard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=320)

**Prerequisites**
member of the Ulfen Guard; Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36); Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

**Access**
At least one of your parents is Ulfen.

</column>

---

Central to your Ulfen Guard training is the ability to protect an ally. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) skill feat for [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. You gain the Designate Ally action.

It’s anathema for you to abandon your designated ally or allow your designated ally to die when you can prevent it. If you violate this anathema, you lose the ability to Designate Ally and any feats that use this ability until you spend 1 day of downtime reaffirming your dedication to your allies. 

**Designate Ally** <actions string="Single Action" /> Choose an ally you can see, who becomes your designated ally. For the next minute, whenever your designated ally is adjacent to you and you’re conscious, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saving throws. You can have only one designated ally at a time, and if you designate a new ally, the previous ally loses any benefits.

<title level="2">Ulfen Guard Dedication leads to...</title>
[Defender's Grit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7736), [Guard's Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=7737), [Guarded Mind](/Feats.aspx?ID=7738), [Protective Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7741), [Reactive Striker](/Feats.aspx?ID=5084), [Tight Follower](/Feats.aspx?ID=7740), [Wounded Party](/Feats.aspx?ID=7739)

>
[Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1171) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**There is a more recent version of this, [click here to view.](/Feats.aspx?ID=4858)**

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 77, [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 151

</column>

---

Your experience keeps you on your toes, allowing you to adapt to even the most dangerous challenges. When you gain a fighter feat using combat flexibility, you gain three fighter feats instead of one. The first feat must still be 8th level or lower, the second feat can be up to 14th level, and the third feat can be up to 18th level. You can use the first feat to meet the prerequisites of the second or third feats and the second feat to meet the prerequisites of the third feat. You must meet all feats’ prerequisites. In addition, you can adapt to the battlefield’s challenges by spending 1 hour to train. If you do, you can reselect the feats chosen with combat flexibility as if you had made your daily preparations.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 127

**Prerequisites**
[improved flexibility](/Classes.aspx?ID=7)

</column>

---

Your experience keeps you on your toes, making you adaptable to even the most dangerous challenges. When you gain a fighter feat using combat flexibility, you gain three fighter feats instead of two. While the first feat must still be 8th level or lower, the second feat can be up to 14th level, and the third feat can be up to 18th level. You can use the first feat to meet the prerequisites of the second or third feats and the second feat to meet the prerequisites of the third feat. You must meet all feats' prerequisites. In addition, you can adapt to the battlefield's challenges by spending 1 hour to train. If you do, you can reselect the feats chosen with combat flexibility as if you had made your daily preparations. You can't trade out limited-use abilities that you've already used, such as Determination.

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

Your mercy transcends the bounds of life and death. When you use Mercy, you can cast [_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=395) on a creature that died since your last turn to return it to life. **Access**

---

You have a talent for making friends through simple kindness, often among stray animals or other creatures that people tend to overlook, and your inherent magic can make these acts take on additional power. As an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action, you can feed a small treat, such as a millet dumpling, to an animal that has an indifferent or better attitude toward you. For the next 1 minute, one of the animal’s unarmed attacks becomes a +1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) unarmed attack. If it was already a +1 striking attack, it instead gains the effects of the [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) rune.

</column>

---

Nobody pays attention to the gardener keeping the hedges, the maid serving the food, or the dirt-covered worker eating in the corner of a tavern. You have mastered the ability to be an unassuming presence wherever you are. When you Impersonate a laborer, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception checks and DC to avoid others detecting your deception, it only takes you 1 minute to assemble the disguise, and you don’t need a disguise kit to do so. You can’t use this feat’s benefits to Impersonate a specific individual.

**Trigger**
An enemy you’re [observing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84) attempts to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) an ally you can also observe.

</column>

---

You move with unbelievable alacrity to intercept an enemy’s attack. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); [stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) twice directly toward the triggering enemy. If you end within the attack’s range or reach, you become the target of the triggering Strike, using the original attack roll and comparing the result to your AC. If the enemy’s attack fails and the enemy is within your reach, you can immediately attempt a melee Strike against the enemy at mythic proficiency.

</traits>

**Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 69

</column>

---

Your connection to elemental wood manifests as resilience—towering trees, rough bark, deep roots, and patient determination. You gain the Unwavering Resilience reaction.

**Unwavering Resilience**<actions string="Reaction" />** Trigger** You attempt a saving throw against a [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, but you haven’t rolled yet. **Effect**You tap into the power of the Plane of Wood, gaining strength and mental fortitude. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus on the triggering save. If you critically succeed at this saving throw, you become bolstered by your success; blossoms and new growth temporarily sprout all over your body, and you gain a number of temporary Hit Point equal to your level. These temporary Hit Points last for one minute. When there temporary Hit Points are lost, the verdant growth subsides.

You and your megafauna companion are bound together; as long as you live, it's much harder for your companion to die. If your megafauna companion gains the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition, it automatically succeeds at the recovery check to stabilize at 0 Hit Points on its turn. Additionally, your megafauna companion only dies at dying 5 rather than dying 4. Finally, the first time each day your megafauna companion would reach dying 5 and die, as long as you're still alive, your companion's dying value decreases to 0 instead.

<title

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"

[Unbreaking Castle](/Feats.aspx?ID=7303) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 84

**Requirements**
You’re wielding a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12) or a weapon with the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait.

</column>

---

You’re the bulwark that doesn’t break. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316) or position the required weapon to parry; for the next minute, whenever you Raise a Shield or position a weapon to parry (including when you first use this ability), all allies you can see gain the shield or weapon’s circumstance bonus to AC. When your shield is raised or your weapon is positioned to parry while this effect is active, enemies treat all squares within your reach as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). When using the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction, after the block is complete, you can attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a [shield bash](/Weapons.aspx?ID=395) or an attached weapon on the required shield (such as a [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=396) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=397)) against an adjacent enemy at mythic proficiency.

>
[Unburdened Iron](/Feats.aspx?ID=4393) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 44

</column>

---

You've learned techniques first devised by your ancestors during their ancient wars, allowing you to comfortably wear massive suits of armor. Ignore the reduction to your Speed from any armor you wear.

In addition, any time you're taking a penalty to your Speed for some other reason (such as from the encumbered condition or from a spell), deduct 5 feet from the penalty. For example, the [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12) condition normally gives a –10-foot penalty to Speed, but this feat would reduce it to a –5-foot penalty. If your Speed is taking multiple penalties, pick only one penalty to reduce.

You gain the ability to raise an undead familiar who will serve you as your loyal and sometimes expendable partner as you explore your necromantic magic. You gain a [familiar](/Familiars.aspx). It has the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) trait instead of the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) trait and is immune to [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669). You can choose only one familiar ability per day for this familiar instead of two, and you can’t choose an ability that changes the creature’s trait (such as [construct](/Familiars.aspx?ID=109) or [dragon](/Familiars.aspx?ID=111)). Additionally, this familiar can be targeted by spells and abilities that target your thralls. If you destroy your familiar, you can raise them back to undeath during your next daily preparations.

You gain the services of an [undead companion](/Companions.aspx?Type=Undead) that travels with you and obeys your commands. The rules for undead companions are under [Undead Companions](/Rules.aspx?ID=1690) and utilize those for [animal companions](/Rules.aspx?ID=149).

 Contrary to the usual rules for companions, as an undead master it's possible for you to have more than one undead companion at a time. However, only one of those companions, your “active companion,” follows you during exploration and encounters; the rest are reduced to an “inactive” state that can be easily tucked into an inventory or stored in a nearby crypt. If you ever have more than one undead companion, you gain the Call Companion action, with your undead companions taking the place of animal companions.

    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Undead Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=5721) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Dhampir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=750" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 43

</column>

---

Your knowledge of your own not-quite-living anatomy, combined with your experience in combat, helps you take down undead foes with ease. Against [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures, you gain a circumstance bonus to damage with weapon and unarmed Strikes equal to the number of weapon damage dice for the Strike. This bonus increases to double the number of weapon damage dice if your target has the [vampire](/Traits.aspx?ID=778) trait.

    right="Feat 2"

>
[Undead Slayer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3474) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 28

**Archetype** [Undead Slayer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=174)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Your training has prepared you to recognize most [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) on sight. You become trained in two [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skills, each about a specific type of undead, or become an expert if you were already trained. You gain the Slayer's Identification free action.

 **Slayer's Identification** <actions string="Free Action" /> **Trigger** You roll initiative and can observe a creature you know is undead; **Effect** You attempt to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) to identify the undead creature with a +1 circumstance bonus. If you're a master in the skill you're using to Recall Knowledge, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus instead.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the undead slayer archetype.

<title level="2">Undead Slayer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blessed Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=3475), [Frighten Undead](/Feats.aspx?ID=3479), [Gear Up](/Feats.aspx?ID=3480), [Hunter's Sanctum](/Feats.aspx?ID=3476), [Necromantic Resistance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3477), [Slayer's Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3478)

[Undead Spotter](/Feats.aspx?ID=5240) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Wake the Dead #4](/Sources.aspx?ID=219) pg. 28

</column>

---

Your studies of the undead have taught you telltale signs of a disguised undead creature. When you Pursue a Lead that involves a corpse or creature within your reach, you can touch that corpse or creature to immediately determine if it is undead. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Recall Knowledge checks about undead creatures and to determine if a creature is undead.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Verduran Shadow](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=312)

**Prerequisites**
[Verduran Shadow Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7606)

</column>

---

You gain the [Terrain Stalker](/Feats.aspx?ID=5224) feat, selecting the underbrush [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2365); if you already have Terrain Stalker for underbrush, you can select a different type of [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). If you [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622) while exploring, and if any allies use [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=2625) to follow you as you do so, you can extend your Terrain Stalker feat’s benefits to one ally so long as they remain within 10 feet of you. If you have master proficiency in Stealth, you can extend the effect to two allies. If you have legendary proficiency in Stealth, you can extend it to four allies.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Underground Network](/Feats.aspx?ID=2156) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 209

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14); [Streetwise](/Feats.aspx?ID=846)

</column>

---

You're connected to groups that know what's going on in the streets, and you can get information out of them quickly. When you use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) in an area where you have a network (typically a settlement where you've spent at least a week or spent a day of downtime to build a network faster), you can contact a member of these groups to get information directly from them. This usually takes about an hour, and it doesn't draw as much attention as Gathering Information in public might. The check and information gained otherwise follow the normal rules for Gather Information.

 In addition, if you have successfully consulted the underground network, you get a +1 circumstance bonus to the next check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) you attempt about the subject you were Gathering Information on, or a +2 circumstance bonus if you're using [Underworld Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) for the check. The GM might change the Lore skill related to the network depending on your location or the specifics of the network you're tapping into.

    right="Feat 2"

[Underhanded Assault](/Feats.aspx?ID=1784) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 134

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271) (Level 4)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

You capitalize on the distraction provided by an ally. You [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) up to a foe adjacent to one of your allies. You can roll against the foe you're Sneaking up on, even if it's currently [observing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27) you, as though you were [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22). You take a –2 penalty on your [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check. If your Stealth check against the chosen foe succeeds, you can make a melee Strike against that foe at the end of your Sneak.

<traits>

---

Your mythic power allows you to take a small amount of food and replicate it near endlessly. When you attempt a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) check to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368), you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to attempt the check at mythic proficiency. Succeeding at the check always provides enough food and shelter for you and up to a dozen other creatures. On a critical success, all creatures you obtain food and shelter for gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saving throws for the next 24 hours.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 119

</column>

---

Your senses are finely tuned to the slightest variations in the air, so much that you can place your shot exactly where you intend to aim it from any range possible with your weapon. When attacking with a ranged weapon in which you have master or greater proficiency, ignore the penalty from its range increment. (The weapon's maximum range is unchanged.) In addition, if your target has cover against your attack with such a weapon, it doesn't gain the bonus to AC if it has lesser cover, gets only the bonus of lesser cover if it has standard cover, or gains only the bonus of standard cover if it has greater cover.

[Unexpected Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=993) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=80" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 32

**Trigger**
You would take damage from an attack, spell, or other effect.

</column>

---

Your supernatural connection sometimes causes you to phase from reality when under threat, disappearing for split seconds before reappearing—often surprising you as much as your enemies. Roll a DC 16 flat check. On a success, you gain resistance to all damage equal to your level against the triggering effect, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that effect until the start of your turn, and you gain the [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) condition for 1 round.

<title level="2">Unexpected Shift leads to...</title>
[Fortuitous Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=998)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Unfaltering Ranks](/Feats.aspx?ID=9443) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Bugbear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=744" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=642" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 31

**Prerequisites**
[Friend Of Fear](/Feats.aspx?ID=9429)

</column>

---

You know all too well the dangers of succumbing to fear, and you know how to remove this weakness from your allies. Attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check, comparing it to the Will DC of allies in a 60-foot emanation who can hear you. Each of them is temporarily immune to this ability for 10 minutes.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The ally gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice your level that remain for 1 round. The ally gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to their Speeds for 1 round. Reduce the ally’s [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) value by 2. If the ally wasn’t frightened, they instead gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against fear for 1 minute.

**Success** The ally gains temporary Hit Points equal to your level that remain for 1 round. The ally gains a +5-foot circumstance bonus to their Speeds for 1 round. Reduce the ally’s frightened value by 1. If the ally wasn’t frightened, they instead gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their next saving throw against fear they attempt within the next minute.

</column>

You have witnessed hundreds of fighting styles and quickly adapt to defend against complicated maneuvers. You were forced into service as a laborer, either pressed into indentured servitude or shackled by the evils of slavery, but you've since escaped and have trained to ensure you'll never be caught again. Whenever you roll a success on a check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) or a saving throw against an effect that would impose the [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) condition on you, you get a critical success instead. Whenever a creature rolls a failure on a check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) you, they get a critical failure instead. If a creature uses the [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) ability on you, it must succeed at an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to grab you instead of automatically grabbing you.

---

You can bring back the recently deceased, but at what cost? You add [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1645) to your dirge and can cast it as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell. However, when you [Cast this Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), the returned creature gains the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) trait. (The creature knows it will return as undead when it decides whether to return.) Only powerful magic such as a [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual can return the target to true life again. You gain an additional spell slot each day at your highest rank of necromancer spell slots. You can prepare only the _raise dead_ spell in this slot.

---

Thanks to your powerful speeches, your movement finds allies in all sectors of society and even across enemy lines, all eager to help you accomplish your goals. If you spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) when you use [Ultimatum of Liberation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357), you can ask four questions related to that creature, as if you succeeded at four [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) checks. This information comes to you over the course of the next 1 to 2 hours, representing tidbits of information you glean from local supporters. After receiving this information, the first time you roll [Initiative](/Rules.aspx?ID=3300) in an encounter with the target of your Ultimatum of Liberation or their allies, you and all your allies can make your Initiative check with mythic proficiency.

  • **Animal** Your hide thickens, granting a +1 circumstance bonus to AC.

You can’t use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405), as normal for sources of obvious concealment.
  • **Object** Your skin transmutes partially into an inorganic substance, granting [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to your choice of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
  • **Vegetation** You trigger an accelerated growth, gaining [fast healing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2322) 5.

**Prerequisites**
[Thaumaturge's Demesne](/Feats.aspx?ID=3723)

</column>

---

You can move your demesne here and there, bringing it wherever your journey takes you. Your demesne expands to a maximum of 10,000 square feet. Once per day, you can call your demesne forth, which takes 1 minute. This has the effects of [_resplendent mansion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=257), except that it conjures your demesne from its previous location, with all the benefits of Thaumaturge's Demesne in addition to the those of the spell. You must be able to claim the new area, with the same restrictions as Thaumaturge's Demesne.

---

You gather your curse around you and impel it to pour outward, expanding your maelstrom. The radius of the emanation of your curse maelstrom state increases by 5 feet until the end of your curse maelstrom state. The outpouring of the curse is unnerving. You attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) a creature within the emanation of your curse maelstrom; you don't take penalties for not sharing a language with that creature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 185

**Archetype** [Archer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=238)

**Prerequisites**
[Archer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6252); Expert in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)

</column>

---

With a quick use of brute force, you remove an obstacle and take a calculated shot as part of the same motion. Attempt to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) one adjacent creature, then make a ranged Strike with a bow or crossbow you're wielding. The Strike is made at the same multiple attack penalty as the Shove or Trip attempt, and this activity counts as one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

<traits>

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You can understand the true meaning of texts quickly, and even when you get lost or hit a dead end, you aren’t discouraged from making further attempts to get to the bottom of things. When you Decipher Writing, you need only half as long as usual (reducing the time from about 1 minute to about half a minute per page), and if you fail, you don’t take the usual –2 circumstance penalty to further checks to decipher that text.

[aloof firmament hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=7); [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged, and you're wielding a one-handed weapon in the sword group.

</column>

---

Honed through 10,000 battles, your sword’s mere light can shatter ambitions and break armies. Make a melee [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with a sword, with a spell that isn’t a [cantrip](/Traits.aspx?ID=550) or [focus](/Traits.aspx?ID=511) spell. Countless copies of your sword, made of light, fall around you, dealing damage equal to double the spell’s rank to each creature within a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of the target, excluding you and the target of the Spellstrike. The damage is of the same type dealt by your sword Strike and is treated as [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) and [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920).

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 107

</column>

---

You can create extraordinary—albeit volatile—alchemical wonders, though they have an unfortunate tendency to violently explode when you use them. When you use [Quick Alchemy](/Actions.aspx?ID=2), you can create an alchemical item from your formula book whose level is up to 2 higher than your advanced alchemy level. You can spend up to 3 additional batches of infused reagents when creating this item to stabilize it. Upon activating the item, attempt a DC 10 flat check; for every additional batch of infused reagents you spent to create the item, reduce this DC by 2. On a success, the item functions normally. On a failure, the item explodes, dealing force damage to the user equal to twice the item's level (doubled on a critical failure).

fields.text: Feat 10 Unstable Concoction Alchemist Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 107 You can create extraordinary—albeit volatile—alchemical wonders, though they have an unfortunate tendency to violently explode when you use them. When you use Quick Alchemy, you can create an alchemical item from your formula book whose level is up to 2 higher than your advanced alchemy level. You can spend up to 3 additional batches of infused reagents when creating this item to stabilize it. Upon activating the item, attempt a DC 10 flat check; for every additional batch of infused reagents you spent to create the item, reduce this DC by 2. On a success, the item functions normally. On a failure, the item explodes, dealing force damage to the user equal to twice the item's level (doubled on a critical failure).

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 67

</column>

---

You can mix a wondrous yet volatile liquid into an [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528) [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) if it has an initial effect that uses dice. You [increase the size of any dice](/Rules.aspx?ID=2305) for the item's initial effect by one step. For instance, you could increase damage from a [moderate alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3287) to 2d10 or healing from a [moderate elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308) to 5d8+12. Because this affects only initial dice, it wouldn't increase unarmed attack damage from a [bestial mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3315), [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) from an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3286), and the like. When this item is activated, the creature activating it must succeed at a DC 10 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) or take acid damage equal to the item's level.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Deviant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=426" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gatewalkers Player's Guide (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=287) pg. 10

</column>

---

You shift your body into a higher gear, your speed compounding further and further. You gain a +10-foot status bonus to all your Speeds, which lasts until the end of your next turn. At any time during your next turn, you can use Unstable Gearshift again, increasing the status bonus by another 5 feet and prolonging the effect for another round. You can keep using Unstable Gearshift in this way until you can no longer use your deviant abilities.

While you are in the stance provided by Immovable Object, you ignore [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and greater difficult terrain. Once per 10 minutes, if you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) your Immovable Object stance, you can Stride as a free action. Each creature within a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 14d6 force damage (basic Reflex save against your class DC). Creatures that fail the save are also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

You have become a brutal, unstoppable force of nature, able to shrug off mortal wounds with ease. You gain resistance equal to 3 + your Constitution modifier to all damage, and your resistance from raging increases to 8 + your Constitution modifier.

 In addition, if you are reduced to 0 Hit Points while raging, you can end your rage as a reaction to stay at 1 Hit Point. If you do, you become [wounded 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) (or increase your wounded condition by 2 if you are already wounded).

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 264

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

Your medical training extends to less obvious conditions. When you succeed against a DC 20 check to Treat Wounds, you can also reduce the value of one clumsy, enfeebled, or stupefied condition on the patient by 1. If you’re able to treat more than one creature at once, choose only one to gain this benefit. A creature can benefit from Unusual Treatment only once per day.

If the condition results from an affliction, the affliction isn’t cured, though the condition is reduced as long as the affliction remains at that stage.

If you are a master in Medicine, add the drained condition to the list of conditions you can remove if you succeed at a DC 30 check. If you are legendary in Medicine, you reduce the chosen condition by 2 instead of by 1.

>
[Unwind Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3653) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #180: The Smoking Gun](/Sources.aspx?ID=125) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Clockwork Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=184)

**Prerequisites**
[Clockwork Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3645)

**Requirements**
The target's body must be mostly intact.

</column>

---

Combining necromancy with the mysterious temporal powers of clockwork, you wind a creature backward from the moment of its death. Attempt a DC 40 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check to revive a dead creature that has been dead for no more than 3 rounds. If you succeed, the target returns to life with the effects of [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=243), except it still has the [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) condition it had before dying, increased by 1 (or wounded 1 if it wasn't wounded before dying). Whether you succeed or fail, the target is then temporarily immune to Unwind Death for 1 day.

---

When you cast _humanoid form_ or _illusory disguise_ to alter your appearance, the spell's duration is 2 hours. At the end of the duration, you can extend the spell's duration for another hour, but doing so is taxing, making you [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). You can keep extending it in this way, increasing your drained condition by 1 each time, to a maximum duration of 6 hours.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=113" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 183

**Archetype** [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200)

</column>

---

You draw the _[Ursine Avenger Hood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2368)_ over your head and its fur over your arms, assuming an ursine form that has traits of your original form as well as that of a bear. In your ursine form, you gain a jaws [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage and a claws unarmed attack that deals 1d6 slashing damage and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) trait. Both unarmed attacks are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group. You lose the ability to speak complex sentences while transformed and can only communicate through grunts and gestures; this prevents you from using effects that require a shared or spoken language until you revert back to your non-hybrid form. You can use this action while transformed to remove the hood and return to your original form.

<title level="2">Ursine Avenger Form leads to...</title>
[Fearsome Fangs](/Feats.aspx?ID=4093), [Great Bear](/Feats.aspx?ID=4091), [Immortal Bear](/Feats.aspx?ID=4095), [Terrible Transformation](/Feats.aspx?ID=4092)

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 33 --- The moon has always been connected to the tides, and now you can grasp that connection. You can create massive amounts of water and control these tides, subverting even the moon's sovereignty over the oceans and seas. Choose an area 50 feet long by 50 feet wide within 500 feet, and choose two different effects from the options provided below. The effects take place in the listed order.
  • **Flood** You create a pool of pure, clean water in the area, which coalesces from ambient moisture. This water must be created on a surface—not in air—and flows normally.
  • **Control** You tug on the moon to raise or lower the level of bodies of water in the area by 10 feet. If you control a portion of a larger body of water, the water then equalizes normally.
  • **Modulate** With a wave of your hand, you create or smooth ripples, making all bodies of water in the area either calm or turbulent. Making it calm turns [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) or greater difficult terrain to calm water, and making it turbulent turns calm water into difficult terrain.
  • **Slow** By exercising your rightful control over all water, each creature with the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait in the area must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) (or slowed 2 on a critical failure).
Flood and control are permanent and non-magical. Modulate and slow last until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain the impulse to continue them.

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102); Uzunjati affiliation; master in a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) skill

</column>

---

You tell a quick story or begin telling a longer tale. This is most useful when you want to prove your scholarly credibility or impress someone quickly. Roll a check with a skill that can be used to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) in which you have expert proficiency, using the result entry for the [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59) action. Like Performing, Storytelling rarely has an effect on its own, but it might influence the DCs of subsequent Diplomacy checks against the observers—or even change their attitudes—if the GM sees fit. This action is not a Performance and cannot be used in place of anything that requires you to Perform.

<title level="2">Uzunjati Storytelling leads to...</title>
[Adept Storyteller](/Feats.aspx?ID=7756), [Cautious Word](/Feats.aspx?ID=7757), [Uzunjati Recollection](/Feats.aspx?ID=1114)

This is most useful when you want to prove your scholarly credibility or impress someone quickly. Roll a check with a skill that can be used to Recall Knowledge in which you have expert proficiency, using the result entry for the Perform action. Like Performing, Storytelling rarely has an effect on its own, but it might influence the DCs of subsequent Diplomacy checks against the observers—or even change their attitudes—if the GM sees fit. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Slithering](/Sources.aspx?ID=41) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Oozemorph](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=84)

**Prerequisites**
[Oozemorph Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2185)

**Trigger**
You fail (but don't critically fail) a saving throw against an effect with the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait.

</column>

---

You cause your eyes to liquefy and run out of your eye sockets, leaving them empty. You get a success on the save against the triggering effect, but you are [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for the duration the effect would have had on a failure. At that time, your eyes regrow and your normal vision returns.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vampire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3545) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 58

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
You were a killed by a vampire drinking your blood.

</column>

---

You're a newly risen vampire. You gain the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and [vampire](/Traits.aspx?ID=242) traits and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694), and your undead hunger is for the blood of the living. Your incisors elongate; you gain a fangs [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. They're in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits. You gain revulsion and sunlight vulnerabilities detailed in the Vampire Vulnerabilities sidebar and the Drink Blood ability.

 **Drink Blood** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Requirements** A [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), or willing creature is within your reach; **Effect** You sink your fangs into that creature and drink its blood. This requires an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the victim's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed, and automatically succeeds for any of the other conditions. If you succeed, the creature becomes [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), and you gain temporary HP equal to the target's level that last for 10 minutes. Further uses against the target don't increase the drained condition or grant you more temporary HP.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the vampire archetype.

<title level="2">Vampire Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bat Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=3552), [Clinging Climber](/Feats.aspx?ID=3546), [Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554), [Daywalker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3549), [Manipulative Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3547), [Nocturnal Kindred](/Feats.aspx?ID=3548), [Predatory Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=3550), [Turn to Mist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3553), [Vicious Fangs](/Feats.aspx?ID=3551)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vantage Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3263) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121)

**Prerequisites**
[Sniping Duo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3258)

</column>

---

You and your spotter take advantage of each other's attacks to momentarily hide and throw your foes off-balance against your follow-up attack. When you successfully make a ranged Strike against a foe, your spotter can use a reaction to attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against the foe's Perception DC. On a success, the foe is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against the spotter's next attack before the end of your spotter's next turn. Similarly, when your spotter successfully makes a ranged Strike against a foe, you can use a reaction to attempt a Stealth check against the foe's Perception DC. On a success, the foe is flat-footed against your next attack against them before the end of your next turn.

---

You adjust your innovation's core, changing the way it explodes. When you choose this feat, select acid, cold, or electricity. Your innovation's core runs on that power source. When using the [Explode](/Actions.aspx?ID=902) action, or any time your innovation explodes on a critical failure and damages you, change the damage type from fire damage to the type you chose. 

If you have the offensive boost class feature and retrain Variable Core to a different damage type, you can also switch to a different offensive boost that deals the same damage type if you wish.

    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Shades of Blood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #213: Thirst for Blood](/Sources.aspx?ID=257) pg. 84

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42)

</column>

---

Using the power of your own blood, you encourage increased blood flow to nourish damaged tissue or stifle the flow to clot wounds or prevent the spread of poison and disease. You no longer require a healer’s toolkit to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396), [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=2397), [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=2398), or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), though you take 1 damage each time you take one of these actions without the proper tools from the expenditure of your blood. You can’t reduce or prevent this damage.

You gain a +1 item bonus when performing these actions using your blood, which increases to +2 if you’re a master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) and +3 if you’re legendary.

---

You are adept at designing and maintaining mechanical [vehicles](/Vehicles.aspx), and you lavish your attention and ingenuity on one vehicle in particular. You become an expert in Crafting, and you choose one vehicle you own—or your party owns collectively—to be your signature vehicle: the vehicle you spend time customizing to grant it various advantages. You can spend 1 week of downtime with a new vehicle to designate it as your signature vehicle instead. Due to your amazing customizations and adjustments, pilots gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any piloting checks they make to control your signature vehicle. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2.

You can spend 1 week of downtime with a new vehicle to designate it as your signature vehicle instead. Due to your amazing customizations and adjustments, pilots gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any piloting checks they make to control your signature vehicle. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the mechanic archetype.

[Efficient Controls](/Feats.aspx?ID=8653), [Engine Bay](/Feats.aspx?ID=8650), [Impervious Vehicle](/Feats.aspx?ID=8654), [Miraculous Flight](/Feats.aspx?ID=8655), [Patch Job](/Feats.aspx?ID=8651), [Superior Propulsion](/Feats.aspx?ID=8652)

You’re able to shift yourself into the spaces between to avoid notice. You gain the Part the Veil action.

**Part the Veil** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are not observed by any enemies; **Effect** You phase yourself into the interstices, veiling yourself from physical reality. You become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). You can use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) as your disassociation from reality makes you difficult to focus on. If you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251), this effect ends after the action is complete; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute.

Born of a blood hag, a fiery blood drinker hidden behind a false skin, you have one blood-red eye and the ability to slough off your appearance in an instant. You gain the [Lie to Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=811) skill feat, and you can shed a disguise quickly by peeling off the outer layer of your skin. Changing from a disguise used to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) back to your true appearance is a 3-action activity for you; if you're an expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), it's a 2-action activity, and if you're legendary in Deception, it takes only a single action. This doesn't allow you to don or remove armor or other equipment any faster, but your physical appearance otherwise returns to its normal state.

<title level="2">Veil May leads to...</title>
[Invoke the Elements](/Feats.aspx?ID=2337)

You heart aches for vengeance against those who have wronged your people. Choose one of the following dwarven ancestral foes when you gain Vengeful Hatred: [drow](/Traits.aspx?ID=51), [duergar](/Traits.aspx?ID=53), [giant](/Traits.aspx?ID=79), or [orc](/Traits.aspx?ID=124). You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to damage with weapons and unarmed attacks against creatures with that trait. If your attack would deal more than one weapon die of damage (as is common at higher levels than 1st), the bonus is equal to the number of weapon dice or unarmed attack dice. In addition, if a creature critically succeeds at an attack against you and deals damage to you, you gain your bonus to damage against that creature for 1 minute regardless of whether it has the chosen trait.

**Special** Your GM can add appropriate creature traits to the ancestral foes list if your character is from a community that commonly fights other types of enemies.

May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 14 **Archetype** [Harrower](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=204) **Access** This feat is available to all players in a Stolen Fate campaign **Requirements** You have an active harrow omen. --- You manifest a ghostly deck of harrow cards. Draw a card from a harrow deck, then select a target within 60 feet. The card flies through the air to strike at that target, inflicting 4d6 damage, with a [basic saving throw](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) against your class DC. The type of damage inflicted is determined by your active harrow omen; if the card drawn is in the same suit as your active harrow omen, the target takes a –2 status penalty to its saving throw. The damage increases to 6d6 if you're 10th level and 8d6 if you're 15th level. You can continue to throw cards at targets on your turn as long as you Sustain the Vengeful Spirit Deck—throwing a card takes two actions. This effect lasts as long as you Sustain it, up to 1 minute, or until you no longer have an active harrow omen. Once the effect ends, you lose your active harrow omen.

  • **Keys**: fire damage
  • **Shields**: poison damage
  • **Books**: electricity damage
  • **Stars**: mental damage
  • **Crowns**: acid damage

fields.text: Feat 6 Vengeful Spirit Deck Two Actions May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate Uncommon Archetype Metamagic Source Stolen Fate Player's Guide pg. 14 Archetype Harrower Access This feat is available to all players in a Stolen Fate campaign Requirements You have an active harrow omen. You manifest a ghostly deck of harrow cards. Draw a card from a harrow deck, then select a target within 60 feet. The card flies through the air to strike at that target, inflicting 4d6 damage, with a basic saving throw against your class DC. The type of damage inflicted is determined by your active harrow omen; if the card drawn is in the same suit as your active harrow omen, the target takes a –2 status penalty to its saving throw. The damage increases to 6d6 if you're 10th level and 8d6 if you're 15th level. You can continue to throw cards at targets on your turn as long as you Sustain the Vengeful Spirit Deck—throwing a card takes two actions. This effect lasts as long as you Sustain it, up to 1 minute, or until you no longer have an active harrow omen. Once the effect ends, you lose your active harrow omen. You can store prepared venom in your throat and spit it at your foes in addition to your own toxic spray. You can [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to store a dose of injury or touch [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) in your throat; when using this action, you do not risk envenoming yourself as long as the poison is your level or lower. The next time you attack a target with your venomous spit unarmed attack, the poison is expended. If you successfully hit the target, they are exposed to the poison in addition to the other effects of your spit. As long as you are holding venom in your throat, your speech is noticeably difficult to understand. You can hold only one dose of poison like this at a time.
